title: Requested: NPCs and creatures wander, idle and aggro by their own record variables (AI packages, Fight), as the original game does
status: Wander and idle by the record packages are on by default since v0.0.57 (compiled MWScript and npc-ambient.lut). 30 October 2026, v0.0.57 alive branch: levelled creatures now get their own record's Wander package (ACTOR-LEVELLED-NO-WANDER-56) and creatures that wander attack on sight by Fight and distance (OpenMW engageCombat rule, through AW_CombatAggro); in-game check pending. Still open: NPC aggro (disposition), flying and swimming creatures, Alarm. Seen again in v0.0.62-dev1, outdoors as well as in rooms: hostile creatures in the wilderness (the floating scrib, CREATURE-FLOATING-62) do not attack on their own either, so the missing aggro is not limited to the ancestor ghost in the Andrano Ancestral Tomb. Expected, as in the original: the creature's Fight value and its distance to the player decide whether it attacks. Tracker ROOM-CREATURES-NO-AGGRO-62. Which creatures attack in v0.0.62-dev1: blighted rats and the cliff racer attack; the scrib, the ash slave and the corprus stalker do not (CREATURE-BIPED-ANIMS-62, CREATURE-FLOATING-62). 8 November 2026, v0.0.63 branch: the engage check ran only for actors with a compiled Wander package row; an actor without one (no package, a first package other than Wander, or a room creature the place's table does not answer) never attacked on sight. Fix on the branch: such an actor gets a standing slot for the engage check alone when its Fight can reach 100, as OpenMW checks every actor in range. By the game data and its settings (20 and 0.005 per original unit): the scrib (Fight 50) and the guar (70) never attack on their own; the mudcrab (83) attacks within 600 original units, rats and the kwama forager (85) within 1,000, the ancestor ghost, ash slave, corprus stalker, cliff racer, nix-hound, alit and kagouti (90) within 2,000. Not yet seen in game; whether the tomb's ghost lacked a package row is not measured. The ash slave and corprus stalker not fighting back: CREATURE-BIPED-ANIMS-62.

title: Akulakhan's Chamber does not fit in 32 MB of Fast RAM: its room models need more memory than is free
status: 10 November 2026 (v0.0.64-dev4 line): at 32 MB Fast RAM the chamber's room models needed about 18,130 KiB while about 14,780 KiB could be given to them after leaving Balmora, so the load failed and the game returned to Balmora. Releasing memory that can be made again before the load (86c595a5) did not close the gap; the town keeps nothing behind (2,451 KiB free after the return against 2,399 on the first visit). Two thirds of the bytes were the collision of the hollow cave and Akulakhan models with exact standing bevels on every plate. The chamber is now built in three types, picked by the room type setting: 0 exact bevels everywhere (18,579,456 bytes of models, does not load), 1 exact on the near-horizontal plates only (15,621,904 bytes, does not load), 2 approximate bevels everywhere as every solid model (14,142,096 bytes): type 2 loads at 32 MB in 25.4 s with 2,519 KiB Fast RAM free inside and is the default (2c3c5add). A standing-box sweep along every wall found no point where type 2 lets the player further into a wall than type 0; it stops the player a little earlier at about 2 to 6 % of the sampled wall points (mostly 1 to 4 units). Earlier, 27 October 2026: the reported stall was the slow preset plus the room growing its memory twice before the models fitted. Open until the default is in a shipped build and checked in play.
where: Akulakhan's Chamber (the Heart Chamber), entered at 32 MB of Fast RAM
severity_reason: A slow room load at the required memory size; the room does load.

title: Arriving in Seyda Neen, the first frame of play lasts about 13 to 15 seconds; v0.0.59-dev6 test sessions stopped on it as a stall
status: The first play frame after arriving in Seyda Neen took 12.2 to 15.3 s on the dev5 and dev6 engines. Three causes, each measured with the per-frame file counter: the player's assembled body (21 parts loaded in one frame, each opened three times), the compiled scripts' journal names (a 16 KB buffer refilled twice per topic, 6.9 s), and the actor rows (a binary search on disk with a 16 KB buffer, about 1 s). Fixed in v0.0.59: the body's parts load over several frames and stay in memory (aw_player_cache 1, 281 KB), a file is opened once instead of three times, the journal names are read in one pass, the actor rows use a small buffer and recent finds are kept. The first play frame is now about 1.0 s (server 0.36 s, screen 0.38 s); the parts are no longer reloaded later in play, and wearing a cuirass loads one part in 50 ms. Still open: the first frame is above 0.5 s; the parts are not yet one packed file; CHIM chunks (.ccs) are still opened more than once in the load frame.
where: engine/aga aw_view.c player parts at arrival; tools/engine_smoke.py stall check
severity_reason: The game stands still for 13 to 15 s right after arriving; the dev6 test sessions and boot smokes failed on it as a disk stall

title: Long audio DMA gaps lose elapsed playback time
status: 16 October 2026: EClock-based playback clock is in the shipped engine (see AUDIO-DMA-CLOCK-DRIFT-35); native listening after long DMA gaps not recorded.
where: engine mixer (snd_dma.c, snd_mix.c) after long DMA gaps
severity_reason: Playback clock loses wraps after long gaps; not a cure for all crackle, no crash.

history.note: AUDIO-CLOCK-29: long DMA gaps lose elapsed playback time (SOURCE REPAIR CANDIDATE) (part 1 of 2): Where/how: the real `snd_dma.c`/`snd_mix.c` fixture advances a synthetic playback cursor while the game does not poll it. A 16,584-frame gap loses a whole 16,384-frame ring from the inferred clock, records zero late frames instead of 15,482, and does not promptly repaint the current playback cursor. Two-wrap and five-second cases also reproduce the defect. A 120 ms control correctly reports a shorter deadline miss. Cause/correction: counting only observed backwards modulo positions cannot recover complete unobserved wraps. The next source uses the driver's existing EClock-derived absolute sample-pair estimate, exact fractional Paula period rate and double start time. A ring-aligned signed-counter epoch keeps long sessions bounded. Epoch/device-time resets cancel stale channel deadlines, clear old PCM and re-prime through the existing mixer. Tried/results: four focused Linux Docker methods pass, including actual PCM written at the current cursor after long gaps, PAL/NTSC driver clocks, long unpolled intervals, reset/epoch/shutdown, loading and speech preservation. The old scheduler fails three long-gap and two reset controls. New fixtures use sanitizers. Both changed translation units compile for Amiga 68040: three existing pointer-signedness warnings in driver buffer interfaces and none from the scheduler. No host compiler/probe or the maintainer emulator change ran.

AUDIO-CLOCK-29: long DMA gaps lose elapsed playback time (SOURCE REPAIR CANDIDATE) (part 2 of 2): Limits/status: ordinary mix-ahead, DMA/source queues, music state and rendering gates are unchanged. This repairs a demonstrated recovery and diagnostic defect; it is not a verified cure for all crackling. Delivered WinUAE has explicit sound settings while FS-UAE mostly uses defaults, so active backend/override equivalence is unverified. Sealed dev2 is unchanged. Fixed: N. Next development source candidate; native listening pending. First verified fixed version: none. See audio evidence (docs/AUDIO.md).

title: OST crackles under heavy loading
status: Fixed in source on v0.0.52-dev (25 October 2026), not built yet: the first load after the intro movie ran the music dry 1-3 times (v0.0.51-dev3 and the final: 0 late, every other load 0 dry). Cause: the music stream reads its next 16 KiB block only from the frame loop (CDAudio_Update) or as the painter's emergency fill; a load holds the frame loop, and the track restarted after the movie with an empty buffer. Now every load-time mixer update (snd_dma.c S_Update_) also pumps the stream's reads (aw_music.c AW_MusicLoadPump, never waits; not under the movie); tests: music_player_test loadpump, aga_loading_audio_test. To verify: the audio smoke of the next dev build, the first load 0 dry, and the maintainer's WinUAE listen. Before: Corrected 25 October 2026 (v0.0.51-dev, not built yet): the first load's 219-319 ms 'gap' and its dry count in the dev1 and dev2 measurements were the intro movie, which plays inside the New Game load, pauses the music and plays its own sound; the load meter timed the paused music. The meter now leaves the movie out and says so, and names the load step at both ends of the longest gap (a trace of the ticks when it passes 150 ms). Measured again (FS-UAE, 32 MB, the dev2 image with the gate 3891 engine, the same five loads): longest gaps 58 (first load, outside a 4,893 ms movie), 43, 52, 115 (Akulakhan's Chamber, world model to entities) and 49 ms, 0 late. history.note: AW-20260928-01: potential prison-ship exit freeze during intro: Reported on 28 September 2026, initially at 15:21 Helsinki, against the current v0.0.19 work, using FS-UAE 3.1.66. During the introductory prison-ship sequence, attempting to exit through the hatch froze the game. The supplied screenshot shows the interior hatch with the Seyda Neen / E: Enter prompt. At 15:28 Helsinki, the maintainer reported that the second attempt worked normally. The exact restart/retry procedure and how long the first freeze lasted were not recorded. Reproducibility and frequency are not established. The maintainer's exact HDF/executable hashes and full emulator settings were not supplied with this report. Do not infer a cause from the emulator version. Next investigation: Repeat New Game, intro, hatch exit and return cycles; record speech/escort state, transition progress and elapsed load time. Check whether input and the emulator remain responsive during the reported stall.

Emulator launch evidence: The maintainer launched `AmiWind-v0.0.19-FS-UAE.fs-uae` using FS-UAE 3.1.66 on Linux x86-64. The log reports a WinUAE 3300b2-derived core and Kickstart 3.1 A1200 revision 40.68. Full settings and image hashes remain unconfirmed. `schedutil` CPU governor warning: possible emulation frame-rate impact; insufficient evidence for a hard-freeze diagnosis. `my_resolvesoftlink` stub and `res_initcode context = (nil)` were also present; the supplied startup excerpt does not locate the later freeze. FS-UAE's official site lists 3.2.35 as the current release on this date. A comparison run with the same HDF/settings is useful, but upgrading is not a demonstrated fix. Keep the older-version reports open. Primary references: FS-UAE 3.1.66 configuration parser (https://github.com/FrodeSolheim/fs-uae/blob/v3.1.66/src/cfgfile.cpp) and official releases (https://fs-uae.net/).

Memory-lifetime hypothesis (unconfirmed): At 15:36 Helsinki, the maintainer suggested that the prison interior might not be properly released after leaving the ship. This is a valid investigation lead, not an established diagnosis. The native C engine uses explicit memory management. `SV_SpawnServer()` calls `Host_ClearMemory()`, which flushes renderer caches, calls `Mod_ClearAll()` and frees the old level's low hunk to `host_hunklevel`; it also clears server/client state. Some alias models remain in the reusable model cache by design. These source paths establish the intended cleanup, not proof that every retained reference or failure path is correct. Check stale map/actor pointers, cache ownership, allocation failures and memory totals across repeated transitions. The short repeating audio fragment is consistent with the update/mixing loop stalling while buffered audio continues. It does not distinguish memory corruption, a deadlock, an I/O stall or an emulator problem. Do not label either incident a garbage-collection failure or blame FS-UAE without reproduction.

Investigation baseline and limits: Live repository inspected at commit `3305c9861718553acdbec76f825bfad884e0bb94` (v0.0.19). Recovered the matching v0.0.19 private playable, source, handoff and prior emulator harness. Current `engine/` files match that recovered source byte for byte; the current source also compiles for 68040/FPU. Prior v0.0.19 native acceptance focused on music-notice toggling. Hatch/menu evidence was inherited from earlier checkpoints, not an extended soak test. Neither reported freeze has been locally reproduced or diagnosed at the time of this documentation update. No fix for the reported freezes or stability clearance is claimed.

New: QC-AW-FLAME-SPAWN-32 (every `aw_flame` entity prints "not a field" twice, "No spawn function" and an edict dump: the game logic has no `aw_flame` spawn function or fields; 51 per Census office load, 8 per prison ship load), CENSUS-LOAD-SLOW-32 (Census office "Scene ready" 7,816 and 10,320 ms against 0.2-1.5 s elsewhere; load time follows the flame count, likely the console output above written line by line to the session logs; A/B pending) and DEBUG-MAP-SAVE-VALIDATION-32 (after `map vf0291`, `vf2386`, `vf2485` the autosave fails validation; two also report "Interior spawn blocked"). history.note: BALMORA-CAPACITY-005: retained town maps exceed entity admission (part 1 of 2): Observed/version: private v0.0.28-rc1 image001 bounded Balmora output, 3 October 2026, while validating flora without changing existing town meshes. First introducing version unknown; these failures are present before flora. Reproduction/measured cause: original bm001 contains 634 func_wall and 18 aw_npc entities, plus worldspawn/start (654 blocks). Its original BSP has 170 models, 18,426 nodes, 53,119 clipnodes and 4,643,376 bytes. The flora candidate adds no models or sprites and retains these original counters. Original bm020 has 658 blocks, bm028 674 and the bm019 arrival 610. Quakedef MAX_EDICTS is 600; func_wall QC retains a solid persistent edict. This is a capacity failure, not just a world-file-budget mismatch. Separately, the unsigned engine clipnode loader accepts up to 65,520 nodes; the stricter world build clip reserve is 32,767 and remains unchanged in this candidate. Established introducing mechanism: the existing immutable scenery catalogue in aw_scenery.c admits only the balmora alias in Begin/Capture/Link. Bounded bmNNN maps therefore bypass capture and retain func_wall edicts. ED_LoadFromFile already captures scenery before QC spawn and frees each captured edict; its catalogue retains each original BSP model, full pose, rotated bounds and collision through SV_ClipMoveToEntity. No new placement architecture is needed. First version introducing bounded-name mismatch remains unproven.

BALMORA-CAPACITY-005: retained town maps exceed entity admission (part 2 of 2): Source correction candidate: one strict predicate accepts balmora and only bm000 through bm063 in all three guards. Names such as bm064, bm100, bm01, bm000x and unrelated maps remain excluded. No instances are collapsed (the all-map audit found zero exact duplicates), models converted, or caps raised. Worst catalogue is 654 walls against its existing 1,000-placement capacity; every map retains 20 non-wall blocks before player/helper accounting. Root's authorized Linux native validation passed the extended rotated-collision fixture and the late-NPC visibility fixture (two tests). These host native results do not certify target gameplay. Final visibility must include catalogue plus actors/statics; target ABI heap accounting must add capacity*sizeof(aw_scenery_t), including entity_t, two bounds vectors, model index and padding. BUILD-CACHE-TRACE-PYTHONPATH-33: gate 450 found that the new read trace refused reuse of an already reused run when another checkout was on `PYTHONPATH` (the builder's own modules counted as outside code); repaired before merge, with a test in the gate's layout. Both steps now print their parts with time and cores in the build log; the next full build shows whether the gaps are gone. Before: 3 November 2026 (v0.0.59-dev3, 1,351 frames): CHIM world pack 2 min 14 s on one core, CHIM validation 1 min 48 s on 6.0 of 23 cores. Report (2026-10-31, the v0.0.57 release build 2026_10_31_v0.0.57_full-v0.0.57-release_7ff625e, with dca2eb3d and af01f913): the tail from the validation's start to the zone walk's end 160 s (dev5: 273 s): validation 92.6 s at 6.6 cores (dev5 148.9 s at 7.5; its unit-cache key now worked out beside the world build), heap gate 4.1 s, the stats 34.5 s at 18.9 cores beside the zone walk 60.9 s at 20.6 (dev5: stats 23.5 s at 2.0, then the zone walk 88.8 s). Still serial: the pack, 110.4 s on 1.0 core (dev5 136.4 s; serial by design, ids in walk order). Left for v0.0.58: the validation's main process (pickling, the ordered_map poll loop, load_world, measure; see below). Stays open. PERSISTING in v0.0.57-dev5 (full build 095612e9, 2026-10-30): after the world build the tail ran pack 136 s on 1.0 core (serial by design: ids are handed out in walk order), validation 149 s on 7.5 of 24 cores, stats 23.5 s on 2 cores, zone walk 89 s on 15. Fixed in part for v0.0.57 (2026-10-31): the stats run in a thread beside the zone walk, after the heap gate (about 23 s off the tail); and the validation's unit-cache key (pass_cache digests of chim/validate.py, 13.6 s measured cold, about 20 s in the build's profile) is worked out in a thread beside the world build (measured: 13.6 s -> 0.0 s at the validation). Profile of the validation on the dev5 world (cProfile, 23 jobs, 152 s, the same as the build's 149 s): the main process is the limit, not the workers: pickling tasks and results (dump 8.5 s, loads 7.6 s, writes 8.2 s), the shared ordered_map loop (10.6 s own time, 5.4 million future.done() calls), load_world 35 s, measure 25 s, visibility_report 16 s, ownership 16 s, ring_needs 5 s. What is left needs the per-frame cross-checks to return smaller results and ordered_map to wait on completed futures instead of polling all of them (build_parallel.py is in nearly every stage key: a v0.0.58 item). title: An interior light change reran exterior stages: the reuse cutoff refuses a stage when any earlier stage's whole output differs, not the files it reads
status: Open (25 October 2026): v0.0.51-dev3 changed only tools/interior_lighting.py (and the engine). The reuse preflight planned 26 of 43 stages reused, 0 unexpected; at run time 12 of them were refused by the output cutoff (npcs, hands, npc-gallery, world-flora-assets, harvest, hand-catalog, door-audio, character, reading, world-ui, actor-contact, world-terrain), because bsp, census and the other room stages now bake different light. The legacy scene chain is one ordered line (tools/build_parallel.py DEPENDENCIES: bsp, npcs, hands, ... world-ui, actor-contact, world-terrain), and world-flora-assets, harvest and hand-catalog follow census only for its palette (BUILD-PALETTE-RACE-32), yet census.bsp's new light refuses them. The read trace records checkout reads only, never run-folder reads, so the cutoff cannot narrow to what a stage opened. Repair: record each stage's run-folder reads with their SHA-256 and refuse only when one of those differs (whole-output compare kept as the fallback for records without them); the preflight then names the stages that follow a rebuilt stage's outputs as conditional, not as reused Seen again (2026-10-26 00:17 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:17 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try4): an engine change confined to aw_items.h (a parser prototype) and aw_skel.h (the table struct) rebuilt world-flora, chim and chim-town-seyda, whose keys hold every engine header they compile for the struct sizes of their heap checks; the sizes they measure did not change. Key those stages on the measured sizes (compile_target_sizes output) instead of the header sources.

title: A public build can die halfway when the disk fills: the only space check runs once at the start, against a fixed 20 GiB, not what the release really takes
status: Reported by a tester (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26): their v0.0.50 build from the public repository stopped when the disk ran out; the free-space check runs only before the first stage and asks a fixed 20 GiB (AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB), however much the build needs. The maintainer: a gate check from the start, compared with the release s own build size, automatically against the previous known good build with about 20 % extra. Fix: every passing build records its measured full-build footprint (peak bytes of the workspace, the caches and the scratch, per file system); the release ships the last known good build s figure in the repository; before any stage the preflight asks for that figure plus 20 % on each file system and stops with the numbers when it is short; each stage checks its own last measured bytes plus 20 % before it starts; a gate test fails when the shipped footprint is missing or older than the release. The maintainer (2026-10-26 15:20 +0200 / 2026-10-26 13:20 UTC): the margin about 30 % or more, depending on the dependencies; the need counts everything a fresh build takes, not only the workspace: the builder images (about 2.2 GB each), the Morrowind game data copied into the Docker volume, the caches, the storage pool and the scratch. Measured 2026-10-26: the build runs alone take 19 GB (v0.0.51 final) and 16 GB (v0.0.52-dev3), on top of the shared pool and caches. Fix written (2026-10-26 19:45 +0200 / 2026-10-26 17:45 UTC, v0.0.53 builder, branch v0.0.53-disk): tools/disk_need.py. The check runs first in every image build (tools/build.py right after the options are read: build.sh, build.cmd and the build inside Docker), before the builder image is built (tools/build_docker.py, where Docker storage is visible from the host) and before the game data is copied into a volume (tools/run_docker.py, checked inside the image); and before each stage against that stage's own last figure (tools/build_profile.py start). The need per file system: the last known good build's figure (the larger of the shipped config/disk-footprint.json and this workspace's newest passing build) plus disk_margin_percent (30), less the cache and pool when the workspace already holds a passing build's, the workspace never below min_free_gib (35); both in config/build-defaults.json as machine settings that key no stage (tools/build_cache.py keys that file without them; AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB, AMIWIND_DISK_MARGIN_PERCENT and AMIWIND_DISK_WATCH were keyed environment before: now ignored), also --min-free-gib and --disk-margin-percent. Every passing build writes RUN/disk-footprint.json (run folder bytes, scratch peak from the free space sampled every 5 s, cache and pool growth, game data, per-stage peak growth); tools/disk_need.py ship RUN puts it into the repository. First figure, measured read-only on the build volume: the v0.0.52 final's run folder 15.47 GiB (dev3 the same), storage pool objects written in the v0.0.52 cycle 28.84 GiB (an over-count), game data 1.79 GiB, builder image 2.0 GiB: a fresh native build needs about 58 GiB, Docker about 63 GiB. Gate tests: tests/test_disk_need.py (no stage re-keyed by the settings, a stage stops before it starts, a passing build writes its figure, the shipped figure exists and is not older than the release, the guides state the need). Open until a build writes the first measured figure with stage figures. Gate 4048 (2026-10-26 20:14 +0200 / 2026-10-26 18:14 UTC) stopped on tests/test_run_docker (a missing --input-volume must be refused before any Docker run): the volume check now runs right before the game data copy when there is one, otherwise right after the input checks and before the build container is made.

title: Tribunal and Bloodmoon cannot be converted with today's tools
status: Open. Found by the whole-world measurement (every object placed, estimated per map, checked on 30 converted maps). v0.0.64 line: the build options --dlc (tribunal, bloodmoon, both or none) and --no-dlc choose the expansion layers (default: every expansion found) and the base world keys no longer depend on which expansion files are present (BUILD-GAME-INPUT-KEY-BROAD-64); the exterior cell list and the interior reader take a master list (Morrowind.esm plus the chosen layers' masters). Not yet wired into the stages: no expansion cell is built. 10 November 2026 (v0.0.64): the expansions have their own save-ID ranges. Tribunal and Bloodmoon rooms take IDs from their own bases of 4096 after the base batch rooms (engine aw_maps.h, generated table aw_layer_table.h from config/room-batches-tribunal.json and config/room-batches-bloodmoon.json, both empty for now); the engine always carries all three lists, so one engine serves every combination, and an ID in an expansion range the table does not name is titled "needs Tribunal" or "needs Bloodmoon". The disk layout planner moves the expansion stores (chimsol, chimiti, chimibm) as whole units like the interior store. No world or content stage of the base build changes: the reuse preflight against the v0.0.63 release build rebuilds the same stages as before the change (only the engine and the image name the new files). Still open: converting the expansions. Open. Found by the whole-world measurement (every object placed, estimated per map, checked on 30 converted maps).

title: Hard disk buffer and MaxTransfer defaults depend on the disk type
status: Closed: fixed in source (3dfd5095, gate 10881), shipped in v0.0.66-dev5, confirmed by that build's image step, which set 150 buffers on the boot partition and 40 on the world partition from their longest name lookups. Measured on the v0.0.66-dev6 image (FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast, JIT) (the disk layout of v0.0.66-dev5): the 150 buffers of the boot partition and 40 of the world partition cost 72 to 73 KiB of Fast RAM, free memory after a load against the v0.0.66-dev4 image, the same steps: Balmora 2,010 -> 1,938 KiB (largest block 1,938 -> 1,865), Balmora again 1,978 -> 1,906, Vivec 1,396 -> 1,323 KiB (largest 1,342 -> 1,270); the program hunk is unchanged. The sound loads that the buffers serve are on IMAGE-LOADS-SLOWER-66. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev5. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev5 (3dfd5095, 15 November 2026): the image step sets every partition's buffers in the partition table, sized to the partition's longest name lookup (+10, in steps of 10, at least 30, at most 500; tools/ffs_chains.py), reads them back with the drive and records them with the lookup figures in build.json. Measured on the v0.0.66-dev4 layout: the boot partition gets 150 (longest lookup 140 header blocks after the chain relink of IMAGE-LOADS-SLOWER-66), the CHIM world partition 40; before, every partition had rdbtool's 30. MaxTransfer stays at the partition table's 0xFFFFFF.
where: disk images written by the builder (partition buffers, MaxTransfer)
severity_reason: Players and benchmarks silently get different disk defaults depending on the disk type.

The load times in play are measured on the v0.0.66-dev6 image, which has the disk layout of v0.0.66-dev5: see IMAGE-LOADS-SLOWER-66. This replaces the v0.0.66-dev5 report's "not measured yet".

title: A stage whose last real run restored its units from a cache was reused after the code those units come from changed: chim-room-batches kept actor models of the old animation tables
status: Found 2026-10-26 06:29 +0200 / 2026-10-26 04:29 UTC in dev1-try11 (28046c31, reusing try10): the image step stopped on Room batches collide with the image: progs/a_*.mdl and .tag staged with other bytes. chim-room-batches was reused (fingerprint fdd5a1e1, unchanged) although 28046c31 changed tools/skeletal_actor.py and tools/npc_anim.py, which bake its residents (prepare_area.populate): both files are in its closure, but the key covers only the functions its last real run called, and that run restored its residents from the resident unit cache, so the changed table functions (game_table, table_choice, table_groups) were never called and are not in the key. The area stage, which baked, rebuilt with the new tables; the two wrote the same actor names with different bytes. Worked around in dev1-try12 with --rebuild-stage chim-room-batches. Fix: a unit restored from a cache counts the code its unit key covers as called (the unit cache environment digest becomes a stage input), or a stage that restores units keeps the whole module closure of the code that makes them. Fixed in source (2026-10-26 07:48 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:48 UTC): a pass or unit cache keeps the trace lines of the code its key covers (pass_cache.covered_lines: @path TAB unit for each function its key reaches, =path for a file it keys whole) and on its first hit in a process appends them to the stage trace (note_covered); build_cache.used_record keys an = file whole, also when some of its code ran ('=' joins TRACE_MARKS). A stage that takes its residents from the resident unit cache now has the table code in its narrowed key. Tests: test_pass_cache (a hit writes what the key covers, once), test_build_cache (a file a cache keyed counts whole). To confirm: the next dev build after a table-code change rebuilds chim-room-batches without --rebuild-stage.
where: tools/build_cache.py stage keys (function-level units); tools/chim_room_batches.py residents
severity_reason: A reused stage installs stale outputs; dev1-try11 stopped in the image step 20 min in (it can also pass unseen when no other stage writes the same names)

title: The pool map that hands results back in input order scans every held future on each turn: the main process works O(n squared) while large maps run

With a cost every item is submitted largest first, so pending holds every result not yet handed back (up to all 1351); each loop turn counts the running ones over all of pending (_running) and builds the wait list over all of pending. title: The Vivec town stage fits its residents onto the frame collision on one core after the resident bake
status: Open. After the last resident is ready the stage runs at 1.0 cores with no output for over 1.5 minutes (15 minutes in all, dev3 took about 10 minutes at 9 cores): the frame collision is loaded and every ground-mode actor is fitted in one serial loop before the first "Actor support" line. Fix idea: print a phase banner and progress, and fit the actors in a process pool (each fit is independent; the fitter is built once per worker), or keep the fitted origins in a unit cache keyed by the actor and frame collision.
where: tools/chim_town.py ground_actors (frame_fitter, then one actor at a time)
severity_reason: Several minutes of a town stage run on one core with no progress output; no effect on the game.

reports.note: Perf guard of the same build: chim-town-vivec_city parallel map build_resident took 146.1 s CPU per unit (6.97 cores, baseline 5.90) for 39 units, was 7.1 s (+1946 %); image parallel map _write_layout_task 122 s for 2 units, was 66 s (+83 %). In dev3 those residents came from the resident unit cache; here 39 were baked, which adds about 95 min of CPU (about 14 min of wall time at 7 cores) before the serial actor fit. Fix idea: find what moved the resident key for those 39 (the same key reach check as the chim and room-actor keys) and split the resident bake per part so one resident does not run for over two minutes.

title: New collision settings re-keyed the NPC, creature, player-body and resident unit caches, which never read them
status: Fixed on the v0.0.64-unitkeys branch. Two causes. (1) The hollow bevels and collision mesh settings were added to mesh_geometry_env.py and collision_source_env.py as top-level constants; import-time code counts in the key of every function of a module, so every bake importing them was re-keyed. They now live in hollow_bevels_env.py and collision_mesh_env.py, and the two modules are byte-identical to v0.0.64-dev4 again. (2) A unit key counted every setting name its reach holds as text, including names held only in a constant no reached code uses, so the model hull default change (chain to auto) would have re-keyed every NPC and creature bake. A setting now counts only where the reached code names it; units stored under the older form are looked up under it and stored again. The residents still read the model hull by their reach (the resident pool key reads mesh_geometry_env whole) and are re-baked. Seen again in v0.0.66-dev1: with the merging reader of the base game and both expansions, every unit cache of the build would bake again in full (2,147 of 2,147 resident bakes, 2,064 of 2,064 scenery regions, 1,931 of 1,931 flora regions, 2,158 of 2,158 player parts, 1,059 of 1,059 room batches and more), also for the cells, rooms and actors the expansions do not change: a unit key takes its stage's whole game input and source closure, not the records the unit reads. The build stopped at its reuse guard after 12 minutes and was run again with the full bake allowed for 13 stages. Seen again on the v0.0.66-dev1 build (13 November 2026): the new merging reader of the expansions is in every unit key, so with the expansions switched off (the same data as v0.0.65) all 1,769 room batches bake again, about 14 to 16 seconds each, about 7 hours, besides 12 more stages. Wanted: a unit keyed by what the reader gives it for the masters loaded (the decoded records), not by the reader's code.
where: unit cache keys: tools/unit_store.py, tools/actor_units.py, tools/mesh_geometry_env.py
severity_reason: The v0.0.64-dev5 build stopped at its reuse check: about 3 hours of bakes would have run again; no effect on the game.

reports.note: The release build: the Vivec room stage bakes its 269 room residents again after the world step (about 20 s a unit against 0.32 s reused, about 85 min at 24 cores), the same wide resident key as the room batches earlier in the same release.

the v0.0.66-dev1 build (base game only) baked all 1,769 room residents again (about 7 h) because the merging reader of the expansions is in every unit key, though its output for the base game alone is the base game file itself

on the v0.0.66 line after the dev1 build: a default-off parameter added to the shared skeletal bake (only the creature models pass it) and a module text edit in the NPC library re-keyed all 2,147 room residents, 2,342 room actor fits and 423 NPC appearances with no change to their output; listed with their old keys (unit_store.LEGACY_SOURCES), compared unit by unit

the v0.0.66-dev2 build stopped at its reuse stop on 16 stages (resident-bake 0 of 2147, interior-room 0 of 198, interior-room-chim 0 of 1059, player-parts 0 of 2158 and more): module-level lines and signature defaults count as import-time code of every unit key that reaches the module, so a new constant (the skin row limit), a new default-off parameter (the skin fit) and a new constant in the room stage (a record field name) re-keyed units whose output did not change

the v0.0.67-dev3 line checked against the v0.0.67-dev2 build: all 2,342 room actor fits would have run again. A fit reads a room through three readers of the room conversion (tools/chim/interior.py), so its key held the whole import-time code of that module and config/chim-rooms.json, which a default value there names; the everywhere recipe in the rooms added one module line and one room setting, neither read by a fit. The fits of 40 rooms (247 placements) of the dev2 image are byte-identical with the dev2 tree, the dev3 line and the fixed tree; the readers moved unchanged into tools/chim/room_records.py and the fits stored before are found again

Seen on 23 November 2026 from the other side: the player parts, first-person parts and animation table caches key their tool files' import-time code only, so a change inside a bake function leaves the stored units in use, while a change to the known-missing parts list bakes every player part again.

title: An engine build can stop on the warning that the generated CHIM version header is shorter than expected
status: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker GAME-RECORDER-61, a side finding). One of three engine builds with --check-profiles on the v0.0.61-recorder branch stopped with "build/version/chim_version.h is shorter than expected" in sv_phys.c. Cause: the heap header's make rule runs the version generator on every make (its heap-size-check prerequisite is always out of date), beside the compiles, and the generator rewrote amiwind_version.h, chim_version.h and amiwind_version.i every time, so a compile could read one half written. Repaired on the v0.0.61-recorder branch: the generator writes each of them only when its text changed; tests/test_aga_native_source.py checks that a second run leaves them untouched.

title: Bitter Coast trees (flora_bc_tree family) look like a pyramid trunk with a flat box floating above it
status: 2026-11-10, branch v0.0.64-fence2: the renderer now has a see-through face kind. The converter marks every texture whose alpha channel leaves at least 1 % of its texels under half alpha (name prefix "{", palette index 255 for its transparent texels; other textures keep their bytes and unit keys), and the engine draws those faces in a separate pass after the walls, z-tested, skipping index 255 (aw_fence, dbg fence; off by default until a measured A/B on the next full build decides). Proof pending: the cobweb in Andrano Ancestral Tomb and a hanging growth outdoors with the switch off and on. Bitter Coast crowns that use see-through textures are covered by the same pass; their geometry is unchanged here. Earlier: Open: cause unknown; proposed fix direction: crossed vertical planes with the tree's outline (alpha kept), angle impostors as the alternative; A/B first, nothing built. Seen again in v0.0.62-dev1 (PERSISTING): Bitter Coast trees with fungi growing on them are drawn as a distorted stand-in, a dome-like shape at flora_bc_tree_08, taken from its collision-only model, so the bracket fungus (Hypha Facia) beside it floats in the air (FUNGI-FLOATING-62; the earlier floating-tree fix BC-TREE-FLOATING-60 covered trees that did not reach the ground, a different fault). Decided direction: (1) a tree whose parts can be picked or touched gets a very low-polygon solid trunk with measured dimensions, no part thinner than half its original width and no new gaps (the method in the mesh reduction notes, MESH-REDUCTION-SEAMS-62); (2) purely decorative foliage can be transparent planes or sprites; (3) fungi are seated on the trunk surface.

title: The cave piece shared by in_moldcave_21, in_mudcave_21, in_pycave_21 and in_lavacave_21 has a non-convex face, so its collision falls back to the piece chain in every room that uses it
status: Open (24 October 2026): seen by the maintainer in the v0.0.48-rc1 build log and present since dev2 try 13. All four meshes are one geometry packet (6db52335d50b7e51) with different textures; the collision compiler refuses it every time with "CheckFace: Found a non-convex face (error size 0.802837, point: -64.906250 67.406248 -45.484377)", also after the coplanar-facet merge retry, and the builder falls back to the piece chain (19 times in dev2 try 14, 11 so far in rc1). The rooms still build and pass their heap gates; the cost is larger collision data per room and a longer room stage. Single meshes do the same less often (dev2 try 14: in_ar_shellbottom_01, in_ar_shelltop_01, in_ci_01, in_v_arena_01; rc1: ex_vivec_c_02). Fix: weld or split the one bad face of that packet before the union (a planar tolerance for faces off by under a unit), so the union compiles.

A new builder option, `--chim-model-bevels exact` or `tol:N`, adds the bevels, off by default: over the models of every frame's heap peak it grows the hull planes from 3.2 to 3.9 million (tol:4) or 5.8 million (exact) and puts 8 to 40 frames over the CHIM zone budget. title: Entering Akulakhan's Chamber when it cannot load stops the game with an error at the console instead of refusing at the door
status: 10 November 2026 (v0.0.64-dev4 line): a room that cannot load no longer stops the game; it returns the player to the place they came from (Load failed ... Returning to balmora). The chamber itself now loads at 32 MB with room type 2 (AKULAKHAN-CHAMBER-32MB-STALL-53). The heart of the chamber is placed and drawn, as a fixed resident with its idle frames only, so it cannot yet play its Death1 animation when struck (ENDGAME-CHAMBER-COLLAPSE-63). Earlier history: Cause found and fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (24 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing: 32 MB got no automatic cache bank (CHIM-AUTO-BANK-CLIFF-51), so the room's 10.1 MiB of models did not fit. With the repaired engine dbg tp heartchamber at 32 MB loads the room in play (365 placements, 135 models, 5.0 s). Open part: a room that cannot load during play still stops at the console instead of refusing at the door PERSISTING in v0.0.52-dev2 (2026-10-26 11:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 09:18 UTC, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB, image 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev2_dev2_3715e8c4). Seyda Neen, then Balmora (dbg cam recall bm3), then dbg tp heartchamber ended in Host_Error: CHIM room map maps/rifa4ef181ed.chim: its room record or models cannot be loaded. The room found 2 MiB of the free Fast RAM for its models (and 1994 KiB of the Hunk) and a model of the store could not be loaded. Afterwards: Memory now 4795 KiB free, largest block 4492 KiB. Loaded as the first map it works: 4 MiB taken, Memory now 1291 KiB free, largest block 1177 KiB, zone 1476 KiB free. The difference was the skeletal session memory held since the town: the animation tables and the large pose cache, 1589 KiB. Fixed in 2d49fb88 (gate 4032): before Chim_RoomGrow measures the free Fast RAM, the engine flushes its skeletal models from the model cache and gives back the tables and the large pose cache, all made again on demand (aw_skel_release.c). Checked on a play copy of the dev2 image with the 2d49fb88 engine swapped in: the same route loads the chamber (1589 KiB given back first, 3 MiB of Fast RAM and 1994 KiB of the Hunk taken, room 148 models 18129 KiB loaded in 2701 ms). Afterwards Memory now is 2200 KiB free, largest block 2058 KiB; the zone has 420 KiB free, largest run 417 KiB. The Heart's structure and a figure before it are in view. Still open at 32 MB: 2 model loads fail both after the town and as the first map (zone failed requests, the last 250624 bytes after the town, 60112 as the first map); at 64 MB 0 fail. Which models these are (Dagoth Ur's full model and the Heart's actor are the suspects, outside the build gate's count) is not identified yet. Stills: clips/v0.0.52 akulakhan_chamber_32mb_after_balmora, 32mb_first_map, 64mb_after_balmora. 2026-10-26 12:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 10:53 UTC: named and fixed (v0.0.52, gate 4034). The two failed loads at 32 MB were not models left out: zone failed: model 1639 (x/ex_dwrv_enter00, a Dwemer entrance of the room, 250,580 bytes) and model 4991 (i/in_akulacave00 tile 5,8, 147,092 bytes) are the requests that made the room grow (try 1 full, the free Fast RAM bank; try 2 full, the Hunk rest; try 3 loaded): every model was in place (room: 148 models, 18,129 KiB; zone used = the gate's need), neither Dagoth Ur (an actor model in Quake's cache, not the zone) nor the Heart. The console now says so (room: loaded whole on try 3; it grew 2 times, each after a request the full zone refused). The real shortfall was the margin: after Balmora the room bank was 3 MiB (zone 420 KiB free) because the tables given back do not join the largest block and the bank was cut to whole MiB. Fixed: the room bank in 64 KiB steps (CHIM_ROOM_GRAIN); a registry of re-makeable session memory (aw_fastrelease.c AW_FastReleaseRegister/AW_FastReleaseAll, 8 releasers, one console line each with free and largest block before and after) called before the CHIM cache banks at start-up, -chimcache and a room's growth (never per frame), the skeletal tables and posed frames its first releaser; a console line of the free Fast RAM at the room step. title: Travelling from Seyda Neen to Balmora sometimes hangs on the Loading screen (boot smoke, 2 of about 5 runs)
status: Open, in the test sessions only (they serve the remote console from a host folder mounted as a drive; a player's game has no such drive). The cause read from the emulator's source on 16 November 2026 and shown in a test session the same day. The three stops examined with the packet read off the game's stack on the v0.0.66-dev10 image were all requests to the test sessions' remote-console folder, a host folder FS-UAE serves as a drive from a host thread: an open answered not found, a write of 320 bytes completed, an open for output completed; each finished on the host side with its results in the packet, every handler idle, the game asleep on its reply. In FS-UAE 3.1.66 that host thread announces a completion by setting one bit of a shared interrupt-request word with a plain read-modify-write, and the emulator thread clears another device's bit of the same word the same way on every interrupt-request change (a2065.cpp rethink_a2065, before its configured check); an overlap loses the announcement, no dummy message reaches the handler, and the finished request stays on the handler's private queue. Upstream made these operations atomic in December 2016; the 3.1.66 line does not have it. Players have no such drive. Way out for the sessions: deterministic = 1 (no host thread for host folders), asked for by tests/sessions/load_repeat_hops_det.txt; the stall examination now prints the handler's state word of the stuck request (-1 = finished by the host side, the handler never told). title: Roads and paths on the ground look blocky: each texture square is drawn with hard edges instead of blending into its neighbours
status: Reported 18 October 2026 by the maintainer (the road paths look poor at present; every path of the game): a path breaks into separate squares instead of reading as one track. Morrowind's land texture layer is 16 x 16 squares per cell and blends neighbouring squares; ours draws one texture per square with hard edges. Planned A/B, first option the maintainer's (20:04): (d) DIAGONAL SPLITS: where a square's texture meets a different texture on two adjacent sides (a corner of a stair-step edge), split that square along its diagonal into two triangles, each with one texture, so stair-steps become 45-degree edges (marching-squares over the texture grid; about one extra face per split square, no new textures). Then, if needed: (a) baked transition textures for the edge pairs that occur, (b) a dithered edge band baked into the surfaces, (c) finer squares along roads. Measured in faces, memory and frame time; OpenMW at the same pose.

title: A Shield effect on the player does not lower the damage of the blows that land on the player
status: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker INVENTORY-ARMOR-RATING-61, found there). OpenMW 0.51 mwclass/npc.cpp getArmorRating adds the Shield effect's magnitude to the armour rating, and a blow landing on an actor is reduced by that rating. The player's combat sheet (aw_combat.c AW_CombatPlayerSheet, aw_inventory.c inv_combat) holds the worn pieces and the unarmored rating only, so a Shield changes nothing in a fight; the inventory window's rating (AW_CombatPlayerArmorRating) already adds it. Planned: the same magnitude added where a blow on the player is reduced, read at the blow (the effect can start and end during a fight).

severity_reason: a defensive spell has no effect in a fight; the rest of combat is unchanged

Both on by default since v0.0.57. In-game check pending.

title: The game froze once on dbg tp balmora issued 6 s after dbg tp prisonship
status: Open, cause unknown, seen once in FS-UAE (dev3 image, remote console on), not reproduced in two more attempts: the remote command was taken, then picture, state file and console log stopped while the emulator kept running 2026-10-10: suspected same mechanism as HANG-IDLE-DUSK-35.
where: dbg tp balmora 6 s after dbg tp prisonship, remote console on
severity_reason: Freeze; debug path only.

history.note: CENSUS-LOAD-SLOW-32 cause; REMOTE-CONSOLE-LOG-COST-32 and DEBUG-TP-SHIP-FREEZE-32: CENSUS-LOAD-SLOW-32: cause confirmed in one FS-UAE container (loaded machine, relative numbers): dev3 Census 8.8-20.9 s with the remote console on, 0.13-0.16 s off; normal play is not affected. New: REMOTE-CONSOLE-LOG-COST-32 (each console line costs about 7-18 ms with the remote console on; test sessions only) and DEBUG-TP-SHIP-FREEZE-32 (one freeze on `dbg tp balmora` 6 s after `dbg tp prisonship`, not reproduced in two more attempts). The game logic repair for QC-AW-FLAME-SPAWN-32 is in source on a later branch, not in v0.0.32.

Cause attributed on 17 November 2026 (v0.0.67-dev1 line, the load fallbacks job): the same mechanism as CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43, captured on 16 November 2026. With the remote console on, every console line and every state-file write of the test session is a request to the remote-console folder, a host folder the emulator serves as a drive from a host thread; FS-UAE 3.1.66 announces a finished request by setting a bit in an interrupt word that its emulator thread rewrites without atomic operations, so now and then the announcement is lost and the game sleeps on its file reply for ever. The freeze of 8 October 2026 shows each sign of it: the remote console was on, the game stopped right after it had taken a command from the command file (the state file was no longer rewritten), the emulator ran on at full speed, and no key or console line reached the game; the load itself never began (no heap line of a new load). Not captured in a debugger, so attributed, not measured. A player's game has no such drive. The game side cannot catch it (its main loop itself waits for the reply); the test sessions' way out is the deterministic mode of CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43. A load whose frames run but whose arrival never comes now ends after a time limit with the OK box (LF7, docs/LOAD_ERRORS.md).

title: With a graphics card installed the engine picks an RTG screen, then draws it through the slow generic path: the direct CyberGraphX copy is switched off
status: From a tester s minimal RTG patch (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26; private copy, not merged): VID_Init opens cybergraphics.library and, when it is there, asks BestCModeIDTags for an RTG mode, so is_cyber_mode is set; VID_Update then sends the frame through WritePixelArray8 (a one-row planar bitmap per rect) because the direct WritePixelArray RECTFMT_LUT8 call is inside #if 0, and that disabled call passed rects->width as the source modulo where the buffer row (vid.rowbytes) is right. The bootcheck also refuses a machine without AGA. Not confirmed on our side yet: needs the virtual graphics card (UAEgfx) with Picasso96 on the emulated Amiga. Scope (roadmap, RTG beside AGA): AGA stays the default where AGA exists; RTG when there is no AGA or when chosen; the upload from Fast RAM (not drawing into card memory) is the design the roadmap measures first.

title: Equipping the iron shardaxe is refused while the iron longsword can be equipped
status: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker PLAYER-GEAR-VISUAL-59). With one iron shardaxe carried, equip is refused ("Diagnostic inventory equip refused."), while the iron longsword is equipped at once. Cause: the inventory catalogue marks a weapon or shield as one the engine can equip only when it has no enchantment at all, and the iron shardaxe carries a Cast When Strikes enchantment. The same rule refused 191 weapons with Cast When Strikes, 59 with Cast When Used and 20 shields with Cast When Used in the v0.0.61-dev1 catalogue. Fix on the v0.0.61 line (the catalogue step, tools/prepare_inventory.py): a weapon or shield whose enchantment does nothing while it is merely held (Cast When Strikes, Cast When Used) is equipped as any other; only a worn item's Constant Effect enchantment is an active effect (OpenMW 0.51), and those stay refused until constant effects are applied. The strike effect itself is not cast yet: WEAPON-STRIKE-ENCHANT-NOT-CAST-61. Test tests/test_inventory_assets.py. Checked in game on a Seyda Neen MiniWind image built from the fix (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): the iron shardaxe is equipped at once, held in the right hand, drawn in first person and in third person, and unequipped again. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build.

status: Open. Expected, as in the reference engine: activation takes the nearest object along the view ray within the activation distance, tested against the drawn body, never the nearest character. history.note: Cause found in v0.0.67: the person under the crosshair and a load door behind him were chosen by two separate tests (the door test looks through people), so both names were drawn on one spot under the view and the use key opened the door instead of talking. Fixed in source on the branch v0.0.67-uilayout: one focus a frame, the nearest thing along the view ray among the person's box, the item or plant, the load door and the hinged door; the title, the action line and the use key all follow it, so what is shown is what the use key does. Host tests by number: a person in front of a door, an item between the player and a person, an item beside a body, a mushroom inside a person's box. Not yet checked in play.

Seen in a session from the v0.0.67-dev2 opening journey's quicksave: from the census office's street door's arrival point (eye 259 41 70), aiming at the door 113833 (31.7 units along the aim, within the activation distance), the use key went to Fargoth (128964) in 5 of 8 aims although he stood 37 units away at 228.7 62.5: the aim started inside the box the use pick takes for him (0 to 21 units along the aim). The pick takes the drawn frame's box (aw_scene.c AW_NPCTargetReach), but his model holds one stored frame with its animation beside it (progs/a_70b3ebc9daa8.mdl: 1 frame, its range -23.5 to 39.4 by -40.2 to 36.8 by -2.5 to 33.9 model units), so every animation frame falls back to frame 0 or, when the model is not in the cache, to the whole model's bounds, far wider than his body (7.3 units half width).

Seen again in the opening journey with the engine of gate 11463 (v0.0.67-dev2 image): from the census office's street door's arrival point (eye 255 39 70), the use key went to the Seyda Neen guard (128967) standing at 260.5 57.8, 19 units from the eye and 47 from the door, in 4 aims and to Fargoth in 1 before it opened the door on the 7th aim: the aim started inside their boxes (0 to 12 units along it).

Cause of the census office and Guards' Quarters sightings: a person's model has stored one frame since v0.0.52 (skeletal actors: a rest frame and an animation table), and the box of that frame encloses every pose, about 60 units long around a body about 15 wide, turning with the person. The use pick takes the drawn frame's box (the v0.0.60-dev3 fix of CORPSE-INVENTORY-NOT-OPENABLE-59), which never narrowed this kind of model, and the whole model's bounds when its frames are not in memory; that fix's test fixture had two frames, while every person the game shipped had one. Fixed in source on the branch v0.0.67-focusbox: a person whose model stores one frame is met by his body's box, the collision hull's half widths 7.32 by 7.12 times his scale, never wider than the stored box, with the stored height kept so the head stays aimable; the same while the frames are not in memory, once the use test has seen the one frame (a bit it keeps with the model). A body is met by the stored box lowered to 8 units over its floor, so it is searched by looking down at it. Creatures and models with more frames keep the box they had (their own measured width is a follow-up). Host tests by number: Aleri Aren at the door back to the courtyard (the old box met at the eye, 0.0 to 3.6, before the door at 35.5; her body's box is missed and the door wins; aimed at her, she is met at 36.0), and a one-frame fixture beside the two-frame one (beside the line missed, on it met; a body missed level and met looking down). Lesson for the tests: a fixture of the kind the game ships. Not yet checked in play.

title: A recording made while an NPC fights the player does not replay the same: the fight takes a seed of its own on the replay's load

title: With god mode on, a fight's blows still take the player's health and kill the player
status: Checked in part on the v0.0.61-dev2 image on 6 November 2026 at 32 MB Fast: with god mode on, the Samarys ancestor ghost's blows that hit took 0.0 health (three hits), and with it off the same blows took 1.0 to 3.7 health each. Not yet checked: god mode kept across a map load (fact 2 below). Before: Open, v0.0.61; corrected 6 November 2026. Two facts: (1) the combat layer takes a blow's damage on its own fighter sheet and never reads Quake's god flag (aw_combat.c has no FL_GODMODE check), so god mode cannot stop a fight's blows; (2) Quake clears the god flag whenever the player spawns on a map (host_cmd.c), so a teleport or door that loads a map turns god mode off without a word (the original keeps it). The session that showed the player killed ("you have been killed by Guard") had set god mode before a teleport that loaded the map, so fact 2 was enough there; fact 1 is read from the code. Planned: the combat layer skips the player's damage in god mode, and god mode survives a map load.
where: Combat: an NPC's blows on the player while dbg god on is set (Seyda Neen)
severity_reason: scripted in-game checks that rely on god mode end with the player dead

history.note: HANG-IDLE-DUSK-35: cause found: HANG-IDLE-DUSK-35: the idle freeze is a music stream read that never returns while the main loop waits for it, the same call chain as SEYDA-LOAD-HANG-30 (v0.0.30). Linked with the suspected and possible freezes of the same kind; repair (non-blocking music read) in progress.

HANG-IDLE-DUSK-35 game side repaired in source, ENGINE-SYNC-IO-MAIN-LOOP-36: HANG-IDLE-DUSK-35: the music stream reads through asynchronous DOS packets (`aw_aread.c`); a read that is late or never answered is logged once, the music goes silent and the game goes on; the stream resumes on a late reply or is abandoned after 6 s for the next track. Soak verification open. ENGINE-SYNC-IO-MAIN-LOOP-36: the sweep that followed lists the other synchronous file calls during play (CHIM streaming, sound and voice loads, model reloads, autosave, lamps).

CHIM-DEV3-MAPLOAD-CRASH-36 cause and CHIM-WORLD-INDEX-FILE-LIMIT-36: CHIM-DEV3-MAPLOAD-CRASH-36: cause found by an A/B sweep and a build bisect (c8bf614 dies, its parent loads): the asynchronous music reader used the pointer from AllocDosObject(DOS_STDPKT) as a StandardPacket, though it is the DosPacket part, so every music read corrupted memory. Fixed in aw_aread.c, keeping the HANG-IDLE-DUSK-35 behaviour. CHIM-WORLD-INDEX-FILE-LIMIT-36: with that fixed, every CHIM map of dev3 was refused: the engine read at most 4096 world files and the coast world has 7,236. One limit (65535, the 16-bit file field) in the engine and the writer. The dev3 image loads Seyda Neen and Balmora with both fixes.

HORIZON-POP-29: distant scenery pops or breaks up while turning (OPEN) (part 1 of 2): Priority/type: P1 rendering issue reported in the v0.0.28 Ashlands playtest. Introducing revision and a correction for every reported view remain unknown. Evidence/reproduction: retain global 38205 29437 1380, local 335 191 -294, with raw DEG 263 / P -9 and DEG 321 / P -23. Those captures change pitch as well as yaw. A later controlled case uses global 51855 39125 3502, local -348 565 107, raw DEG 265 / P 0. At fixed pose/time, disabling far culling restores distant coverage; restoring it restores the original viewport. Sweep nearby yaw at unchanged pitch and time. Cause established for the inspected central peak, 5 October: the missing silhouette belongs to the authored opaque static `terrain_rock_rm_18`, not LAND alone. Source placement/transform and ray intersections identify it. The whole rock's bounding sphere fails the forward-distance visibility gate at this camera. A LAND-only horizon fill therefore cannot reproduce its taller silhouette. This attribution does not establish every horizon report's cause; the earlier bounds/PVS checks remain limited to their sampled scene. Rejected correction: a bounded heightfield remesh combining LAND with large rocks fails coverage, false-sky-occlusion or conservative-depth gates in 44 of 48 sampled views. Its worst top-silhouette error is 13 pixels at 128x60. This rejects that approximation, not every possible representation within the budget, and is not a global error bound or native acceptance.

HORIZON-POP-29: distant scenery pops or breaks up while turning (OPEN) (part 2 of 2): Latest diagnostic evidence, 5 October: an opt-in exact-geometry probe visually restores the inspected rock silhouette, but is not an accepted production correction. Seven lossless 320x200 PCX captures use the same palette. The first and last OFF baselines differ in 17,565 of 48,640 viewport pixels (36.11%), invalidating exact A/B acceptance for this run. The reported integer origin stayed fixed, but endpoint view angles were not captured. Recovered per-frame telemetry proves yaw changed from264.37 to 268.33 degrees during the fixed-position session. Exact capture-to-sample alignment and pitch/render-eye data are still missing, so this does not establish the cause of every differing pixel or a matched endpoint camera. Next controlled replay: use the existing mouse `sensitivity 0`, set an explicit pose, and record measured view angles at each endpoint. Require two identical OFF baselines before comparing the opt-in geometry probe, LAND-only path and full reference. Preserve near-depth/occlusion and resource gates. Diagnostic switches remain opt-in and are not production defaults. Next correction/gates: preserve the opaque rock geometry or use a source-checked proxy that retains its silhouette and separate topology, including overhangs. Keep near geometry/depth protection, footprint seams and measured triangle/RAM limits. Repeat controlled camera sweeps and depth/ coverage tests before native frame-cost and visual acceptance. Do not treat a larger draw distance or reduced reserves as the fix. Status: source attribution established; the latest exact comparison fails baseline stability, so no complete horizon correction is accepted. Fixed: N. Candidate: study for v0.0.29. First verified fixed version: none.

title: The inventory character preview does not change when equipment is put on or taken off in the window
status: Fixed in source (709d1399) and shipped in v0.0.61; awaiting confirmation: in the inventory window of a numbered build, each equip and unequip seen changing the character preview at once. Before: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker INVENTORY-EQUIP-CLOTHES-PREVIEW-61). With the window open, Equip and Unequip on a row change the worn set at once, but the preview keeps an earlier picture (seen on v0.0.61-dev1: the bare body with pants, shirt and shoes worn, no cuirass 1 s and 4 s after it went on, the robe kept after it came off; 4 preview renders for 7 changes). The third-person body is right each time. Cause: the parts of a changed outfit load over several frames (at most 40 ms of loading a frame, so that a change never stalls a frame) and the body keeps the previous outfit until they are all in; the window rendered its one picture in the first frame after the change, so of the previous outfit, and kept it. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: the picture waits until the new parts are all loaded (the kept picture shown meanwhile, at most 5 s), then is rendered once, as OpenMW redraws its preview after the new parts are attached; native test tests/aga_inventory_ui_test.c. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): with the window open, the iron cuirass put on, the pants taken off, the common robe put on and the pants put on again each show in the preview 1 s and 4 s after the change, 5 renders for 5 pictures; the third-person body wears the same. The window waited 3 to 8 frames for the parts each time. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build.

title: Map or journal keeps dragging after window focus returns
status: Cause: focus resets did not clear the world-UI drag flag. Candidate passes all 11 sanitizer fixture cases (baseline fails 4). Native focus dispatch untested; no verified fixed version. [Record](BUGS.md).
where: map and journal panels, drag state on focus loss
severity_reason: A drag that ends outside the window keeps panning the map or journal scrollbar after focus returns.

history.note: MAP-FOCUS-DRAG-29: map or journal keeps dragging after focus returns (OPEN): Priority/type: P2 input-lifecycle defect identified and reproduced in a source fixture on 5 October 2026. This is separate from the original map-tab report and the host-to-guest pointer mismatch described below. Reproduction: begin an ordinary map left-drag, teleport-map right/middle drag, or journal scrollbar drag; lose window focus and release the button outside the game; return and move without pressing a button. Expected: the panel stays open but the old drag has ended. The baseline host fixture instead continues panning or invoking scrollbar hit testing after the focus reset. Cause: both native focus events clear gameplay buttons, pending mouse movement and key arrays, but did not clear the world-UI drag flag. Clearing key arrays does not dispatch the mouse-up event that the panel was awaiting. Candidate correction: explicitly cancel that drag on focus loss and gain, alongside the existing input resets. Preserve the open panel, cursor, map view, selected destination and persistent mouse-look setting. No per-frame work, allocation, global sensitivity or button-binding changes are added. Tried/results: a Linux sanitizer fixture compiles the actual map, mouse, gameplay-button and key-reset routines, using the statement sequence extracted from the native focus branch. The four baseline lost-release cases fail; all eleven candidate cases pass. Preservation checks cover normal left/right/middle dragging and release, close/reopen, selection and cursor retention, and clearing pending gameplay motion without an extra move. Actual native focus dispatch and capture transitions remain pending. This result does not close map-tab or physical right-drag acceptance. Fixed: N. Candidate: v0.0.29-dev1 source. First verified fixed version: none.

This marker is distinct from teleporting the player and from the Debug map's teleport control. Expected behavior: map click sets the marker and does not change player position; show the marker clearly on the user map and preserve/update it according to the existing user-marker/save policy. Exact persistence semantics need to follow the current map design. This feature is queued after the urgent torch state handoff repair. No implementation or target acceptance is claimed.

Map interaction requests: The maintainer requests two distinct click behaviors. In normal user-map mode, left click sets/updates a user map marker without moving the player. With debug HUD on, the map should default to DEBUG; in DEBUG map mode, HUD right-click sets the red teleport crosshair and shows the bottom-right Teleport button, with no instant travel. Existing dbg tp map remains available independently of HUD visibility. A debug teleport action must stay separate from a normal user marker. These changes are requested/in progress; native acceptance is pending.

Map controls: source implementation and focused checks: The requested saved cyan click marker, HUD-based default map view, and debug right-click red destination plus explicit TELEPORT confirmation are implemented. The real world-UI/save-codec fixture and input/focus compatibility checks pass in offline Docker. The marker uses three bounded global entries and refuses insufficient capacity atomically. Existing explicit teleport aliases remain HUD-independent. Native acceptance is pending; see WORLD_MAP_AND_JOURNAL.md.

Combined source validation: A fresh combined offline Docker run passed all 80 native-source test methods and the Amiga 68040 build. It includes the UI V2/scene shortcut, full equipment handoff, radius/flame controls, running-torch depth correction, and map marker/ debug selection changes. Native acceptance and delivery of these changes remain pending. The smaller idle-grip defect and scene-specific light/geometry reports remain open.

history.note: MAP-RIGHT-DRAG-29: advertised right-drag does not pan the teleport map (OPEN): Priority/type: P2 input defect identified during 5 October 2026 source review. The teleport picker advertises `R-drag`, but the Amiga input backend sends the right button as `K_MOUSE3` while the panel accepted only `K_MOUSE2`, which is the middle button on that backend. Reproduction: open the teleport picker, place its in-game cursor over the map and hold right while moving. Expected: map pans without selecting or confirming a destination. The baseline source fixture fails to move the map; the corresponding middle-button gesture works. Candidate correction: accept both secondary button codes in the teleport picker and end right-button dragging on release. Preserve existing middle behavior and global bindings. Ordinary map left-drag, left target selection, two clicks without implicit teleport, explicit confirmation and modal exits retain their existing behavior. Tried/results: the focused Linux UBSan comparison reproduces the baseline right-drag failure; its five preservation cases pass. All six corrected cases pass, including release and close/reopen state, with the existing map/journal checks retained. The extended public world-UI fixture and input-event suite pass their two focused Linux methods. Windows and Linux Amiga builds produce identical engine bytes. Manual native right-drag acceptance remains pending. It does not resolve the separate emulator cursor positioning or map-tab click report. Fixed: N. Candidate: v0.0.29 source. title: Mouse cannot switch DEBUG / IN-GAME map views
status: Overlay and event-order fixes pass focused C checks/Amiga builds. Emulator replay shows oversized guest deltas; manual mouse acceptance pending.
where: DEBUG / IN-GAME map view overlay, mouse switching
severity_reason: Mouse cannot switch map views; keyboard unaffected.

history.note: MAP-VIEW-SWITCH-28: mouse cannot switch map views (OPEN) (part 1 of 3): 5 October v0.0.29-dev1 input-path candidate: the native event loop overwrote earlier relative mouse deltas and deferred their delivery until `IN_Move`, while mouse buttons were delivered immediately. Two movements and a click in one event batch could therefore test the previous cursor position. Gameplay also lost earlier movement, and pending/filter state could survive modal boundaries. This source mechanism is distinct from the earlier hidden-HUD gate and does not establish that every reported emulator cursor issue shares it. The candidate dispatches each UI delta before the next button, preserving per-event clamping, and accumulates bounded gameplay motion until consumption. Existing modal/focus button clearing now clears pending/filter motion while preserving the intended mouse-look toggle. Bounded multiplication replaces negative signed shifts without adding allocations or changing sensitivity. Synthetic Linux C checks exercise actual input, map hit testing and modal code: eight corrected cases pass; the baseline reproduces six specific failures and preserves the two ordinary signed/filter behaviors. Separate C99 UBSan checks reject baseline signed shifts and pass the candidate for all three tested paths. Existing gallery behavior passes with mouse events delivered through the real entry point. The public regression suite includes these corrected cases. Windows and Linux Amiga compilation now produces identical engine bytes; the integrated world-UI and mouse-event methods also pass their focused Linux run.

MAP-VIEW-SWITCH-28: mouse cannot switch map views (OPEN) (part 2 of 3): A controlled emulator input trace requested a six-pixel upward host movement but delivered two guest deltas of (+122,+122). From the reset cursor, these deltas are consistent with reaching the footer, whose click branch closes the map; the trace does not log button dispatch or hit-test coordinates. This identifies a mismatch in that input replay; it is neither a successful tab hit nor proof that ordinary manual input has the same defect. Native tab/right-drag acceptance stays open: observe the guest cursor, then test a button without assuming host absolute coordinates equal the game's relative coordinates. Fixed: N; first verified fixed version: none. 4 October v0.0.29 source-candidate update: the DEBUG tab shared the incorrect visible-overlay gate found in teleport-map access. The candidate decouples map controls from HUD visibility and preserves explicit availability and story restrictions. Actual C tests cover DEBUG to IN-GAME and back with overlays off, plus disabled/story refusals; world-UI and console fixtures pass. Input event batching was inspected but not changed. Native mouse acceptance is pending. Fixed: N; source candidate only; first verified fixed version: none. The original unknown-cause/no-repair account below is historical. Reported: 4 October 2026, the maintainer playtest after v0.0.28 release. Clicking the map controls does not switch between DEBUG and IN-GAME views. The supplied screenshot shows both controls, with IN-GAME highlighted. Exact build and emulator configuration are pending; the introducing revision is unknown.

MAP-VIEW-SWITCH-28: mouse cannot switch map views (OPEN) (part 3 of 3): Reproduction to verify: open the map and click DEBUG, then IN-GAME; record pointer position and whether the active view/highlight changes. Expected: mouse selection switches between the two views. Keyboard switching was not reported tested and must be checked separately. Cause: unknown. Proposed investigation: trace mouse event delivery, control hit regions and view-state changes in the matching target build; do not assume a shared cause with the F10 teleport commands. Tried/results: the maintainer tried mouse clicks and reported failure; screenshot inspected, but no independent runtime reproduction or repair attempted. Fixed: N. Repair candidate: none. First verified fixed version: none.

The animations are baked per actor too: every mover holds its own walk, run and attack frames (992 MB of the 1.5 GB of actors in v0.0.51), so the region actors got no movers at all (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35). Design in MODULAR_NPCS.md (docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): a parts library with a few quota levels per part, recipes per appearance, the gallery built from parts (estimate: about 260 s with 4 levels), then one alias model composed per appearance at load time in the engine. Host prototype on v0.0.33-modular-npc: parts baked once with their outfit quotas reproduce the whole bake (6 of 13 Balmora NPCs byte-identical, the rest within 8 faces); not shipped at the time of writing.

history.note: PACKAGE-PORTABILITY-28: source ZIP modes and Windows path aliases: Observed: 4 October 2026, v0.0.28 preparation-helper review on Windows. Rebundling a source tree recreated ZIP entries with mode 0600, losing executable modes. Paths containing alternate-stream colons, reserved device names or trailing dots/spaces also passed lexical validation. No delivered release is known to be affected; the introducing revision is not established. Reproduction/cause: rebundle a synthetic mode-0755 shell entry and inspect its ZIP metadata; submit device/stream/alias names to the path validator. Entry recreation discarded metadata, and the validator checked traversal without excluding Windows filename aliases. Correction and evidence: preserve each source entry's Unix origin and permission metadata; reject nonportable path components and compare case-folded ZIP names on every host. Five interpreted preparation-helper checks pass, including byte/mode preservation, path rejection and the checksum-inclusive size boundary. Actual final-package extraction and audit remain required. Status: preparation-helper correction validated with synthetic inputs; no new game-engine fix or native acceptance claim.
