title: Outdoor cell/sub-cell crossing pauses and lost read-ahead
status: 18 October 2026: for CHIM cells the read-ahead now exists: the cells ahead are read into spare Fast RAM (CHIM-CROSSING-SYNC-LOAD-43, v0.0.43 branch); the legacy region-map read-ahead (aw_cell_change_method 2) stays experimental; one native trace filled 131,072 bytes for the destination, then lost the buffer after high-hunk move failure ([investigation](performance/CELL-TRANSITION-INVESTIGATION-v0.0.29-dev4.md)).
where: Outdoor cell/sub-cell crossing, read-ahead buffer
severity_reason: Crossing pauses and the prefetched buffer is lost; a performance fault.

reports.note: maintainer: crossing between heavy CHIM cells gives a noticeable hiccup; the first presentation of the next frame map loads in the main loop (prefetch work in progress)

history.note: PERF-READAHEAD-29: cell crossing pauses and premature prefetch cancellation (part 1 of 4): 6 October follow-on evidence: one unmeasured sn054-to-sn048 trace filled 131,072 bytes for the matching destination, then recorded high-hunk move failure/free before two copy misses. No prefix bytes were consumed; ordinary loading completed. This attributes one eviction, not its frequency or cost. A caller-specific bottom-gap relocation prototype passes real allocator fixtures and 68040 object/ABI checks. A separate, legacy-behavior gap probe has linked successfully; the observed crossing's actual gap/fit still needs native capture. Both are outside the frozen playtest. No speedup is claimed. See the dated follow-on section in the linked investigation report. Category/status: Performance / Needs work. Fixed: N. First fixed version: none. Investigation and measurement are complete for the bounded route below; no transition-speed fix or accepted speedup is claimed. Report: visible loading pauses interrupt outdoor traversal. Preserve view direction, equipment, active voices and music during optimization. Measured baseline, 5 October 2026: eight automatic sn048/sn054 boundary crossings on the same engine/assets, four per loading method, reached the ready/presentation-callback estimate in 1.070–1.149 seconds. This callback runs after screen update returns and may follow an early return without the destination world being drawn. Thus these numbers are not proven first-world-frame latency. The route used fixed-height noclip to isolate loading, not ordinary walking/collision acceptance. Instrumented model reads consumed about78.9–79.7% of server loading time; measured decode was about4.8–5.2%. The read timer is guest elapsed time inside the model loader, not physical-device throughput. Nested phases overlap and must not be added as independent totals.

PERF-READAHEAD-29: cell crossing pauses and premature prefetch cancellation (part 2 of 4): Read-ahead finding: with128KiB/1.5-second lookahead, method2 filled its prefix on all four crossings, but only one later load reused any bytes (130,948); three prefixes were unconsumed. Both southbound misses match the replayed early target switch; the remaining northbound miss is unexplained. Its approximately30ms lower medians do not establish a read-ahead benefit. Exact source/directory replay shows the southbound endpoint prediction advancing to sn043 before hysteresis allows the actual sn054-to-sn048 handoff, replacing the useful sn048 prefix early. This is a concrete cancellation mechanism consistent with the counters, not native per-frame tracing of the predictor. Source candidate: method 2 now targets the first crossed region; method 1, its default, and the stream reader are unchanged. Four focused C fixtures, a 68040/FPU object compile, and the full 916-test integration suite pass (912 passed, 4 skipped, no failures/errors). These establish source/compile correctness, not patched native performance. Fresh matched native comparison: four counted method-2 crossings per engine, two per direction and two preceding warm-ups, compare the unchanged control with only the first-crossed-region candidate. With 128 KiB and 1.5-second lookahead, prefix use improved from 0/4 to 3/4. Callback medians changed from 1,100.757 to 1,119.780 ms southbound and from 1,154.541 to 1,093.892 ms northbound. This small mixed result does not establish an overall speedup. One fully filled 131,072-byte prefix was still unused. The original method-1/method-2 baseline above is a separate sample set.

PERF-READAHEAD-29: cell crossing pauses and premature prefetch cancellation (part 3 of 4): Next attribution: allocator fixtures demonstrate that hunk pressure can move a resident prefix or evict it before copy. They do not identify the cause of the native miss by themselves. The historical trace proposal aimed to distinguish target changes, explicit cancellation, relocation, eviction and actual copying without changing cache LRU through extra observational lookups. Timestamp limitation: the profile callback runs after screen update returns; that routine may return early without drawing the destination world. Heap audit also precedes this timestamp. Treat 1.070–1.149s as a ready/presentation estimate, not proven first-world-frame time. See the investigation report (docs/performance/CELL-TRANSITION-INVESTIGATION-v0.0.29-dev4.md). Profiler gap: current profiles do not retain predicted-target changes, cancellation/eviction reasons, file-open/seek timing, or transition-scoped audio continuity. The current controls are aw_cell_change_method (1/2), aw_cell_prefetch_kib (128/256/512), and aw_cell_prefetch_seconds (0.5–4, recorded at 1.5). The load TSV records model, method, read bytes/calls/time, decode/world/actor/total times, prefix consumed/read time, low/high hunk, capacity/filled bytes, worst prefetch slice and look-ahead. The visible TSV records model, method, elapsed callback time, requested capacity and look-ahead. These files are appended by AW_StreamLoadEnd and AW_StreamPresented; AW_StreamPresented runs after SCR_UpdateScreen returns and is not proof of a destination draw. Proposed bounded, opt-in instrumentation is described in the report; the later bounded cache-event ring does not implement that entire profiler.

PERF-READAHEAD-29: cell crossing pauses and premature prefetch cancellation (part 4 of 4): Resolution path: extend the matched native route on patched source versus unchanged baseline, with direction and boundary cases, and compare prefix reuse, callback timing, frame cost, and memory. Keep method 1/default unchanged. Do not close this issue merely because the source patch compiles. Acceptance remaining: verified useful prefix reuse and measured latency improvement, ordinary-walking routes, unchanged cell selection/collision, exact view and equipment state, and audible voice/music continuity. The eight baseline crossings retained sampled hands/torch state but did not establish waveform continuity or a comprehensive regression pass.

title: The iron shardaxe in the Seyda Neen pit is drawn but shows no item box and cannot be taken
status: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker WORLD-OBJECT-PLACEMENT-59). The items index lists the iron shardaxe, unowned, in Seyda Neen (-2, -10) at -13088 -74893 102, and the game draws it there, but no item box shows and E takes nothing. Cause, measured in game with aw_placed aim (a check command that prints what the aim test makes of each row near the eye): the axe lies in a dip, about 40 map units below the eye, and its origin is under the ground surface: the line of sight from the eye to the origin stops 8.3 to 8.4 map units short of it (the test allows 6), even with the crosshair 0.8 units from it at 27 units. The aim test only looked at the item's origin: how near the view line passes it (4 map units) and whether the origin itself can be seen; a long item lying with its origin at one end, or sunk into the ground, could not be aimed at. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: a row the placed list draws is aimed at where the view ray enters its model's box, turned and scaled as it is drawn, at the distance of that point, and the line of sight is tested to that point, as the original and OpenMW 0.51 test the activation ray against the object itself; rows the map draws itself keep the origin test. Native tests in tests/aga_focus_pickup_test.c. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast), from 47 game units south of the axe: the ray meets the axe's model at 36.8 map units with the view pitched down 80 degrees, the box shows "Iron Shardaxe, Weight: 30, Value: 100" with E: Take, and E takes it (the world change list counts it taken; the axe is gone from the spot). The gold coin nearby, which the ray misses, is still aimed at and taken through the origin test. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build.
where: Seyda Neen (-2, -10), reference 480636 at -13088 -74893 102
severity_reason: a placed weapon the player should be able to pick up stays out of reach; rooms work

title: When a Fortify Attribute effect on the player ends, the character sheet keeps it as a raised modifier and records the drop as damage
status: Open, v0.0.61. The sheet keeps one modifier per attribute (the race and birthsign fortify) and a damage value. title: The rest window offers Rest in the Census and Excise Office, a cell the game marks as no sleeping
status: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker REST-WAIT-59). The game data marks the Census and Excise Office as a cell where sleeping is not allowed, but in the office the T window opens in Rest mode, and a rest there brings the level-up box; dbg cell there answers that the map has no cell number. Cause: the map does carry its cell keys (_aw_cell_int 763 and its cell ID), but the reader of the map's world entity that dbg cell, the debug HUD and the rest window share stopped at the first value longer than 127 bytes. The compiled rooms (the Census and Excise Office, the Imperial Prison Ship) carry their light grid rows, about 980 bytes each, before the cell keys, so both read as rooms without a cell. CHIM rooms carry no light grid there and were read right. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: a long value is read to its end and kept cut, so the keys after it are found; native test tests/aga_hud_test.c with light grid rows before the keys. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine: dbg cell in the office answers INT 763, "Seyda Neen, Census and Excise Office", and T opens the window with the game line that resting here is illegal and Enter: Wait. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build.

status: 2026-11-10, branch v0.0.64-fence2: the renderer now has a see-through face kind. The converter marks every texture whose alpha channel leaves at least 1 % of its texels under half alpha (name prefix "{", palette index 255 for its transparent texels; other textures keep their bytes and unit keys), and the engine draws those faces in a separate pass after the walls, z-tested, skipping index 255 (aw_fence, dbg fence; off by default until a measured A/B on the next full build decides). Proof pending: the cobweb in Andrano Ancestral Tomb and a hanging growth outdoors with the switch off and on. Earlier: Open, PERSISTING (reported on the v0.0.61 release image and again in v0.0.62-dev1). title: Quickload returns with hands and torch put away
status: Cause established: AWS3 saves store no equipment intent. An AWS4 candidate passes save and compatibility checks; native quickload and integration pending. [Record](BUGS.md).
where: quicksave/quickload equipment state (AWS3 saves)
severity_reason: Quickload returns with hands and torch put away because saves store no equipment state.

history.note: SAVE-EQUIPMENT-29: quickload returns with hands and torch put away: Category/status: Save/load state / Open observation, 6 October 2026. In the exact v0.0.29-dev4 FS-UAE package check, the viewmodel query reported hands state 2 and torch 1 before quicksave. After F9 quickload it reported state 0 and torch 0. Mushroom inventory and picked state survived the same load. Ordinary cell travel uses a separate transient hand snapshot; this report is specifically about restoring equipment at a saved moment. Cause established: the dev4 AWS3 writer records character/story/map state but has no equipment-intent field. The actual save therefore contains no historical hands/torch state for quickload to restore, and the new player starts with zeroed equipment fields. Ordinary travel's transient snapshot does not supply the state omitted from a save. Proposed correction and evidence: an AWS4 candidate adds dedicated validated equipment-intent flags, captures them through the existing transient helper, and restores them before player spawn. It preserves AWS1/AWS2/AWS3 reading, defaults those older formats to unequipped, and rejects malformed or unsupported flag combinations. The original dev4 negative control reproduces the save/restore assertion failure; the candidate passes three save/character/ harvest checks and a global compatibility suite covering legacy decoding, maximum size and malformed inputs. Current gate: the candidate has not passed native quickload or full integration. Verify hidden hands, fists, torch, weapon and weapon-plus-torch across save/load, then confirm compatibility and native behavior. No accepted integrated fix or release is claimed.

With the remote console on, every console print was its own open, seek, write and close on the emulator's remote-console folder, and one "edict" listing is about 300 prints (each field name is padded one space at a time): 1 to 1.2 seconds a listing on a quiet machine, 3 to 7 seconds on a loaded one. The processor samples were idle because the game was waiting on those folder writes. The session wait then called a stall after 1 second whenever neither the game clock nor the engine's ticks moved, although the state file is written only between frames and on the heartbeat; the third session was a 6.8-second frame of script file reads after "dbg mwscript result". Repair: console prints collect in memory and reach the log in one append twice a second (and on the heartbeat, when the 8 KiB buffer is full and at exit), so an edict listing no longer makes a long frame (REMOTE-CONSOLE-LOG-COST-32); the session wait gives a frame without a heartbeat 30 seconds (STALL_GRACE) before the stall examination and logs it as a long frame. Verified: 10 of 10 scripted Seyda Neen sessions (32 MB Fast, JIT) with the same edict prints and "dbg mwscript result" ran without a stop; every script-file frame of 4.6 to 8.4 seconds was logged as a long frame and the session went on. That frame itself is still long and is not part of this repair.

title: The skeletal prototype poses every vertex twice a drawn frame, with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions each: it must cost what a baked frame costs
status: Open (method C, docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the first working version poses an actor s vertices into a scratch frame (bone matrix, quantised with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions, which the 68040 has no hardware instruction for) and the alias path then transforms them again: about twice today s per-vertex work, every drawn frame, estimated at several ms per 1,500-vertex actor on a 25 MHz 68040 (not measured). The method itself costs what baked frames cost: (1) fold each bone s matrix into the one per-vertex transform (view x model x bone, the light direction turned into each bone s space once), so each vertex is transformed once, no divisions or conversions; (2) pose an actor only when its frame changes (alias frames change about 10 times a second, drawn frames 20 to 30); (3) actors on the same table frame share the bone pose; (4) far actors pose less often and skip the joint blend. Acceptance: the frame time of the MiniWind animation stage (SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52) and of CHIM Balmora on the slow-CPU preset no worse than with today s baked actors. Render plan (2026-10-25 22:11 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:11 UTC, after reading AmiQuake s r_alias.c and r_main.c): the actor stays one entity (one box, one light sample, one dynamic light pass, the existing triangle drawing); per bone one combined view x model x bone matrix and the light direction in bone space; the builder sorts vertices by bone so the inner loop keeps one matrix per run (a rigid vertex = a baked vertex s work); pose only on a table-frame change (about 8 a second, a few thousand float operations per actor a second); per-frame ready-made matrices would cost 1.9 to 3.8 MB for the common table and are not worth it; blending between table frames can be switched off (nearest frame). A part that looks wrong rigid and costs too much blended may keep a small shared baked deformation, measured. Progress (2026-10-25 23:46 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:46 UTC): (1) r_alias.c keeps posed frames (8 slots, least recently drawn out; key model, header place, table frame): an actor is posed only when its table frame changes (about 8 a second against 20 to 30 draws) and actors of one model on one frame share the pose; every other draw is a baked frame's work. (2) AW_SkelPoseVerts folds each bone's matrix once with the rest scale and the alias quantisation: per vertex one 3 x 4 transform per bone used, no division; the byte rounding adds 1.5 x 2^23 and reads the mantissa instead of a float-to-integer conversion (the 68040 has no FINTRZ: it traps into the emulation). Native tests within one byte of the builder; compiles for 68040 and 68060 at -O1 and -O2. Not yet measured on the slow-CPU preset (the animation stage). Measured (2026-10-26 05:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:57 UTC, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52): the same MiniWind stage built twice from 7064ea39, --npc-anim-type 1 (baked) and 2 (skeletal). Both ran on the slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 at x14, 49.7 MHz), 32 MB Fast RAM, the Balmora arrival pose at 09:09 with the residents in their own idle (no stage), aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Baked: alias 25.7 ms median (25.6 to 26.0) for 2 alias models drawn, view 1,134 ms, frame 1,261 ms. Skeletal: alias 33.7 ms median (33.5 to 76.0) for 3 alias models drawn, view 1,142 ms, frame 1,271 ms; the 4 lines at about 76 ms are the seconds in which the residents' idle stepped to a new table frame (posing). Per drawn model that is 12.8 ms baked against 11.2 ms skeletal when drawn from the pose cache and about 25 ms when posed. The whole frame was 9 ms (0.7 %) slower at the median and up to 57 ms (4.5 %) slower when posing. Not like for like in one respect: the skeletal build drew one more alias model at this pose (al 3 against 2). Acceptance not met yet: posing costs about twice a baked frame per model. The animated stage (8 actors cycling) on the slow preset is not measured yet. Profiled and cut (2026-10-26 09:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 07:57 UTC). Setup: dbg rcount times the posing (b16bb912: RT_SKELPOSE and RT_SKELVERTS inside the alias time, the kp field with poses made and pose-cache hits), slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 x14), 32 MB, Balmora arrival pose, residents idle, aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Before (b16bb912): one pose was 0.80 ms of bones (AW_SkelPose) and 13.2 ms of vertices (AW_SkelPoseVerts), about 14 ms in all; the vertices are 94 % of it. 871d87e6: a whole frame takes its one key with no blend, square root or division; the never-moving bones are made once per table; the vertex loop has its transforms written out on direct i16 reads. title: A skeletal actor with the full-detail head (about 3,000 vertices) cannot be read: the skeletal block is read only by the alias stream, which takes at most 2,000 vertices
status: Open (method C, docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the first real skeletal actor (a Balmora resident, balyn omavel) is 3,033 vertices and 1,011 faces with the original head (today s default, NPC-HEAD-DECIMATION-33) and 1,398 / 466 with the budget head. The skeletal block (AWSB) is read only by Mod_TryStreamAlias, which leaves models over 2,000 vertices to the generic loader; the builder refuses such a skeletal model by default (vertex_limit 1999). Fix: the generic alias loader reads the block too (or the stream takes skeletal models up to 3,072), with the scratch frame in R_AliasSkelFrame already sized MAXALIASVERTS (3,072). Builder (2026-10-26 00:13 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:13 UTC, --npc-anim-type 2): every skeletal resident and actor-library model is baked with the budget head detail (tools/skeletal_actor.py RESIDENT_HEAD_DETAIL, budget ladder 480..192), so each fits the stream reader's 2,000 vertices; the generic loader is unchanged. Open: the full-detail head on skeletal actors needs the generic alias loader (model.c) to read the block, or the stream to take up to 3,072.

history.note: SKY-GROUND-28: pale ground and excessive cloud speed (OPEN) (part 1 of 2): Observed: 4 October 2026, native WinUAE playtest of the assembled V3 v0.0.28 candidate. The registered Seyda Neen street view displays flat pale ground under textured buildings and the guard. The maintainer also observes cloud motion far too fast. The scripted lighting/camera sequence is a diagnostic, not a normal-gameplay speed or appearance pass. Reproduction: enter the registered town, view the guard and adjacent street in daylight; compare the same camera with fog/cloud rendering disabled. Host geometry, collision and file-readback checks did not expose this defect. Cause: the reconstructed LAND writer emits edge loops with the opposite winding to the native Quake BSP convention. Stored faces and collision remain present, but visible span rendering fails. All 5,597 new LAND faces in the inspected town map differ from the original face orientation. The reconstruction introduced this defect; host checks did not enforce the native winding contract. The earlier zero-winding-change checks proved that clipping preserved input orientation, including the incorrectly authored loops. The new regression checks the native convention separately. Cloud phase combines the persistent 30-times clock with Quake's scroll rate.

This is one third of the preceding `0.01` candidate. Native motion acceptance remains pending. A same-camera native comparison with only the town map repaired and the original engine restores brown textured ground and stone foreground. Fog-off, clouds-off and V1/V3 comparisons retain the ground. The initial combined-engine town replay also shows restored brown ground. history.note: SKY-STARS-28: enlarged stars and night-layer ordering (OPEN) (part 1 of 2): Observed: 4 October 2026, native WinUAE v0.0.28 night views. Bright stars became large slanted diamond-shaped patches over the original night artwork. Disabling `dbg starsky` removed them. Opaque foliage appeared to cover the layer, but fine sprite transparency and both moon silhouettes still require explicit native verification; their failure is not inferred from the report. Cause: the first reduced 128 by 128 composite preserved maximum bright source-star samples and projected each atlas texel over a visible sky area. A bright texel therefore grew to several screen pixels. Combining stars into that atlas also placed them over visible nebulosity. This was introduced with the first combined original-night layer in the v0.0.28 development candidate. Correction: AWN2 adds an explicit 2,048-byte point-role mask; each marked star projects to at most one native screen pixel. The first AWN2 revision removed large diamonds in native views but did not show the intended tiny stars. Of its 136 points, only 20 lay in the sampled upper hemisphere, and doubling the original nebula alpha hid further source stars. The corrected conversion maps the full source square into the valid upper-sky domain and preserves original nebula alpha. Its 163 original-source points all occupy valid upper-sky directions, including overhead, in dark nebula gaps. Black background gaps remain transparent; full moon discs, including unlit areas, cover the field. All sixteen original moon tiles remain byte-identical. Semantic sky depth retains the layer behind terrain, actors and opaque foliage.

SKY-STARS-28: enlarged stars and night-layer ordering (OPEN) (part 2 of 2): Evidence/status: fifteen focused Linux fixtures pass, including two viewport sizes, the full dark moon mask, transparency, sky/world depth and legacy-atlas upgrades. Seven further converter checks cover upper-sky mapping and the revised conversion receipt. Corrected matching target builds and image image015 passed scoped native sky inspection in selected actual-map views. All-map routes and unrestricted world acceptance remain outside scope; stable v0.0.28 is accepted locally within its declared image015 scope.

title: The boot smoke names a stop an emulator disk stall without checking the pending disk request
status: Open. classify() names a stop emulator-disk when every PC sample is in Kickstart's idle loop, the game waits on SIGF_DOS and a word on the game's stack equals another process's message-list address. The label is inferred: a stack word can be a stale pointer from an earlier call, and the active DOS packet, its owner and any pending device request are not checked. What the check establishes is a guest DOS wait with the completion layer unresolved. Next: name it that way, or add the host-side checks (the emulator's queued replies and its interrupt-request flag) to the stall examination; count only confirmed captures against CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43.
where: tools/engine_smoke.py stall.py classify(): the emulator-disk class
severity_reason: sightings counted against CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43 may be other stops; the label decides whether a smoke is retried

reports.note: The first snapshot of v0.0.61 carries the same boot smoke: the stall class is still given from a scan of the game stack, without a check of the pending device request. The page of CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43 lists it among the suspected causes.

history.note: SMOKE-STALL-LABEL-INFERRED-60 seen again in v0.0.61-dev1: the smoke's stall label is a guess: SMOKE-STALL-LABEL-INFERRED-60: the boot smoke names a stop an "emulator disk stall" when the processor sits in the system's idle loop, the game waits on DOS and a word on the game's stack equals another process's message-list address. That is a scan of the stack, not a check of the pending device request, so the label shows a wait on the disk handler and does not show a lost completion in the emulator. The first snapshot of v0.0.61 carries the same smoke. title: A carriable light placed outdoors (a lantern in Seyda Neen) cannot be taken
status: Fixed in v0.0.61-dev2, checked in game on that image on 6 November 2026 at 32 MB Fast: the Ebonheart carriable lantern 132498 is taken with E: its model goes and the world change list holds it (its flame: TAKEN-LIGHT-OUTDOOR-EFFECTS-UNLINKED-61). Before: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker TAKEN-LIGHT-FLAME-61). Survey of the three masters: 130 placements of carriable lights that give light stand in 25 exterior cells of Vvardenfell (Ebonheart 56, Caldera 18, Sadrith Mora 11, Seyda Neen 8, Wolverine Hall 9, Dagon Fel 5, others); Solstheim has 11 more in 4 cells, not in the image yet. Cause: the placed-item list leaves carried lights to the maps, and outdoors the map is the CHIM world, whose chunk placements have no way to be hidden by reference, so the take is refused (an edict, a room placement or a placed item is needed). The same holds for a script Disable of such a placement. Planned: a per-placement reference table for these placements, written at image assembly, so the engine can hide them and keep them hidden after a load.

severity_reason: the original lets the player take these lights; the aim box offers them and the take does nothing

status: 16 October 2026: Coordinate form dbg tp X Y exists and is used in later builds; water-safe arrival not checked in game; fixed version not recorded.

severity_reason: Debug teleport lacked a coordinate form and could land underwater.

history.note: TELEPORT-XY-006: explicit global coordinates and water-safe debug arrival (part 1 of 2): Request/version: the maintainer requested `dbg tp X Y` during unreleased v0.0.28-rc1 development on 3 October 2026. Existing console supported named destinations and the two map-picker aliases, but no explicit global XY form. Source correction candidate: exactly two coordinate tokens, strict finite decimal/exponent parsing with full-token/length/range validation, route through existing AW_MapTeleport/AW_WorldMapTarget, using original Morrowind global XY and existing .25 conversion. Named destinations, no-argument menu, `dbg tp map` and `dbg map tp` remain. Invalid inputs/unavailable destinations do not reset character or world state; extra arguments are rejected. Water cause/correction: old checked map placement landed on submerged terrain. Detect actual water at the standing feet, locate its air boundary with a bounded 20-step search in the loaded local BSP, raise the feet by .25 and recheck the complete standing hull. No assumed zero height or unchecked underwater point. If no air/clear hull exists, placement fails without changing the player pose and the existing checked scene-spawn fallback reports it.

TELEPORT-XY-006: explicit global coordinates and water-safe debug arrival (part 2 of 2): Regression/limits: native fixture sources cover both map aliases, coordinate dispatch, malformed/nonfinite/overflow/underflow/out-of-range/extra arguments, unavailable destination/state preservation, actual water-surface placement and all-water no-solution preservation. Root's authorized Docker native rerun passes all four checks: console dispatch, real-world-resolver scene links, standing spawn/water and Strider available destinations (4 tests, 4.952 seconds). The initial fixture rerun found duplicate resolver linking; the corrected fixture supplies synthetic AWR2 data to the real resolver. Its optional empty Hors preset also required an explicit alive-player precondition, with a new dead-player rejection assertion. No production check was weakened. No emulator screenshot or target gameplay result is claimed. Verified fixed version pending.

title: Samarys Ancestral Tomb has no ghosts, skeletons or other creatures
status: Fixed in source (3ca3d610, gate 8240; the levelled half 4a5778d0 in v0.0.61-dev2) and shipped in v0.0.62-dev1; awaiting confirmation: Samarys Ancestral Tomb seen in play on a numbered build with its ghosts and skeletons. Its five creature references are all levelled lists (in_tomb_all_lev-2, +0 and +2); the room stage lists every one of them as left out ("the pick is not resolved at build time") and the room map carries no entity for them, so the engine has nothing to roll. The engine side of a room's levelled creature (an `aw_levelled` entity rolled from the actor table's lists, CREATURE-ROOM-LEVELLED-54, v0.0.54) is in the game; the room stage that writes those entities was never added. Island-wide in that build: 1,196 levelled references and 478 placed creatures of the built rooms are left out (the placed ones by the default `--interior-creatures listed`, which names four creatures); 84 tombs (408 references) and 63 caves (419 references) place none or one. title: Underwater there is no breath meter and no drowning, and Water Breathing is not applied
status: v0.0.63 release check, round two: an Argonian read Water Breathing 0 at the start, after a load and after a teleport, and drowned in the Seyda Neen bay. Cause found: in the original game data the Argonian race spell "argonian breathing" is a castable spell (Water Breathing for 120 s on self, always succeeds), not a constant ability; OpenMW gives the race's spells to the player's spell list the same way, and a castable spell works only when it is cast. Water Breathing 0 before casting it is therefore the original behaviour; the check expected a constant effect. The engine keeps the spell in the list (character creation, a race change, a loaded game: fix fb279aeb). The in-game check is now: the player knows the spell, casts it, reads Water Breathing 1 for 120 s and does not drown. Cause found in v0.0.64 (round three): the console's sorted id lookup treated a successful read of the actor table as a failure, so player->getspell answered 0 for every spell, also for a player holding the race power; fixed in the engine (the read is checked the right way round), with a test of every call site.

title: Reported viewport/yaw resets while walking or crossing cells
status: Bounded default-off pitch verification is recorded separately below. The broader yaw/transition report and earlier discrepant capture remain open; do not attribute every reset to pitch centering. See [bug tracker](BUGS.md).
where: free-look pitch and yaw while walking or crossing cells
severity_reason: The view resets while walking or crossing cells, disturbing free-look play.

history.note: VIEW-AUTOCENTER-29: forward motion recenters free-look (OPEN) (part 1 of 2): Report: the maintainer reports that yaw/viewport tilt can reset while walking across outdoor cells or subcells, described as a pull toward the default view. Original-engine baseline trial: the recorded control sequence issued `aw_aim 90 -10`, restaged to local position 0,350, issued the same angle command again, then walked forward. A subsequent screenshot showed HUD pitch P:0 at local 0,468/469, still before the next sub-cell crossing threshold. There is no screenshot or angle readback immediately before walking, so this establishes a pre-boundary post-walk discrepancy after the commanded -10 view, not a measured continuous angle trajectory. Source finding: the legacy Quake pitch routine starts automatic centering after forward movement exceeds `v_centermove` (default 0.15 seconds). `IN_Move` also returned immediately when no mouse delta was pending, before stopping drift for held `+mlook`. This matches a plausible pitch-recentering path but is not yet proven as the cause; it does not explain any yaw reset. Design/candidate: automatic centering is legacy Quake behavior and is not an appropriate default for Morrowind-style free-look. The source candidate adds archived `aw_auto_center` defaulting to 0, preserves opt-in legacy walk/lookspring centering, and keeps an explicit `centerview` command. Held `+mlook` stops drift even without new mouse events; a same-frame explicit center command is allowed to proceed.

VIEW-AUTOCENTER-29: forward motion recenters free-look (OPEN) (part 2 of 2): Verification/status: the new Docker fixture passes for the config default and archived registration, opt-in threshold, mid-drift opt-out, explicit centerview after a same-frame quiet-mouse stop (including while +mlook remains held), cancellation by real mouse pitch input, and ordinary quiet-mouse +mlook. Four existing mouse, map, gallery and cell-transition fixtures also pass. Changed 68040 `view` and `in_amiga` objects compile; the `view.c` indentation warning is present in both current and HEAD baseline, while `in_amiga.c` is warning-free in both. This paragraph records the initial source gate; the subsequent native pitch follow-up below supersedes its former pending status. The yaw cause remains unresolved. Fixed: N. First fixed version: none. The dev4 native follow-up now verifies the default-off automatic pitch-centering candidate on a bounded ordinary-walking route and an actual sn037/sn054 crossing. The legacy opt-in still recenters, and explicit `centerview` still works. A later diagnostic replay retained client pitch with drift disabled after an explicit center and fresh aim. The requested -11.25 degrees settles to -9.84375 through the existing byte-angle protocol; that is distinct from a reset to zero. An earlier discrepant HUD capture remains unexplained; no extra behavioral patch was made for it. Actual mouse routines also passed 24 source cases of 600 walking/drift frames each. This establishes bounded pitch-fix acceptance, not closure of every reported yaw/transition reset or an already-delivered dev4.

severity_reason: Unwanted automatic pitch centering; now default-off with legacy opt-in.

title: Native Windows Python geometry-worker queue failure
status: Intermittent invalid semaphore handle; cause unknown; [bug tracker](BUGS.md)
where: Native Windows build, Python geometry-worker queue
severity_reason: Intermittent invalid semaphore handle fails a build; cause unknown.

history.note: WIN-03: Windows image-packing command exceeds process limit — fixed in working tree: Type, cause, symptoms and impact. Deterministic Windows host packaging defect in the v0.0.25 Windows port. All 25 pre-image stages passed, including all 3,551 NPC gallery models and 2,526 world regions. Image assembly reached `tools/world_volumes.py:pack` and failed launching `xdftool.exe` with `[WinError 206] The filename or extension is too long`. The generated terrain partition command contained 6,618 arguments / 165,293 UTF-16 code units, including its terminator, to write 1,651 files. This exceeds Windows' 32,767-unit CreateProcess command-line limit; the message does not mean an individual game filename is too long. The boot-volume command has the same scaling problem. This is separate from WIN-01's intermittent queue handles. Reproduction and evidence. A full native Windows build using normal game content reaches this oversized partition command. Capturing its argument list reproduced the size above; a harmless child-Python invocation with a 40,000 character argument independently reproduced WinError 206. The failed run and completed conversions are retained. Its 1,925 instrumented worker lifecycles reported no invalid handles; that single run does not close WIN-01.

WIN-01: intermittent geometry worker queue failure — open (part 1 of 2): Type, symptoms, cause and impact. Host-side parallel asset conversion on Windows 11, official CPython 3.12.10, in the Windows port based on cloned v0.0.25 commit `3433922c40a48ffd20a0362ed58407298221686a`. Interior, Balmora and Census conversion have failed in geometry work dispatched by `tools/prepare_mesh_bsp.py` through `tools/build_parallel.py:ordered_map`. A worker raises `OSError: [WinError 6] The handle is invalid` inside Python's `multiprocessing/queues.py`, at `self._sem.release()` in `Queue.get`. The queue's semaphore handle is invalid when released; why it became invalid is unknown. The pool reports `BrokenProcessPool`, the stage fails, and the builder cancels sibling work. The Amiga engine compiler passed in these runs. This does not establish a compiler defect, memory exhaustion, or an excessive worker count. Windows cancellation also left orphan workers; process-tree cleanup needs a separate verified correction. Fix or mitigation and validation. No confirmed fix or reliable workaround yet. Retain validated conversion caches and diagnose with separate output directories. Close only identified orphan descendants of a failed build. These are recovery measures, not a fix. Do not disable required content, lower quality or waive validation gates. A future process-management fix must be scoped to Windows, preserve Linux worker behavior, and be validated under the failing workload and a complete build before closing this entry. See Windows build and known issues (docs/WINDOWS_BUILD.md).

WIN-01: intermittent geometry worker queue failure — open (part 2 of 2): Review findings. The observed `Queue.get()` failure occurs after receiving the next task's serialized bytes and before decoding that task. The earlier tracebacks do not show whether the worker had already processed any tasks. Each Windows worker owns a duplicated semaphore handle: ordinary parent-side garbage collection, slow result consumption, or another pool closing its own handles does not by itself explain an invalid worker-local handle. Code review has not identified an executor-lifetime error in `ordered_map`. Instrumented full-run diagnostics now record handle type during deserialization, before/after worker standard-input cleanup, at worker entry, and on queue errors, with the number and identity of previously received work items. These records are private diagnostic artifacts, not release assets. Interpret a failure at startup separately from a handle becoming invalid after geometry work. A handle number reused for another kernel-object type would support a local close/reuse problem; that has not yet been observed. Standard-input cleanup was considered, but the tested interpreter's initial stdin uses `closefd=False`; it remains a low-confidence hypothesis, not an established cause. No automatic retry, alternate multiprocessing backend or reduced-content build has been adopted as a fix. If the failing handle was initially valid, a scoped Windows native handle trace (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/debuggercmds/-htrace) can identify handle-open/close/invalid-reference call stacks. A passing run with different concurrency and cache state cannot alone identify the cause.

WIN-02: cancelled Windows stage leaves worker descendants — open: Type, cause, symptoms and impact. Host process cleanup. Windows stage cancellation currently calls `Popen.terminate()`/`kill()` on the immediate process. Unlike the Linux process-group path, that does not terminate the entire descendant tree. A cancelled gallery left twelve Python workers alive after its parent exited, consuming resources or waiting indefinitely. This is separate from WIN-01; it is not evidence of the semaphore root cause.

title: Cancelled Windows stage leaves child workers alive
status: Fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (25 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing: a cancelled stage ends its whole process tree on Windows (taskkill /T, then /F; terminate()/kill() when taskkill is missing), as the POSIX process group does (tools/build_parallel.py end_process_tree). Host Windows builds only; tests/test_build_parallel.py EndProcessTreeTests
where: Windows stage cancellation in the build scheduler
severity_reason: Cancelled stage left a dozen worker processes alive on the host.

history.note: WIN-02: cancelled Windows stage leaves worker descendants — open: Reproduction. Run independent conversion stages concurrently and cause one to fail while another owns a worker pool. Inspect the cancelled stage's descendants after its parent exits. A synthetic Windows parent/child fixture can test this without game data or disrupting an active build. Fix status. A Windows-only process-tree termination candidate passed the isolated parent/child test, including the virtual-environment launcher. It is not integrated into the public scheduler. A separate candidate also passed a synthetic scheduler forced-failure test; production integration and a full failure-path build remain pending, so this issue remains unfixed. Linux process-group handling must remain unchanged. Until integration, explicitly close only verified orphan build descendants.

title: World objects taken or moved are not remembered: they come back when the cell or room reloads, and saves do not keep them
status: Objects part fixed in v0.0.59 (CELL-CHANGES-59, first slice): one sorted change list for the whole world keyed by a stable reference id (content file and reference number), only changed fields (taken, disabled, lock, stolen mark, moved position, drops), an index by cell, room and scene for map load, no 1,024 or 32 ceiling, kept for the session and saved. Verified at 32 MB Fast on a Seyda Neen MiniWind: an item taken in Arrille's Tradehouse stays taken after another map and after a quicksave and quickload; an item taken outdoors in Seyda Neen stays taken after another map; a bottle dropped outdoors lies there after another map and after a load. Doors, locks and the stolen mark fixed in v0.0.59 (second slice): a hinged door left open stands open when its room or frame comes back and after a load (the census hall door's own saved pose folded in); a lock or unlock by a script, by the console or by the player's key is kept the same way; an owned item taken is recorded as stolen from its owner (the placement's owner, else its faction) by item and owner, so the mark stays with the item through drops, map changes and saves (gold is never marked). Verified at 32 MB Fast on a Seyda Neen MiniWind: the Arrille's Tradehouse door unlocked and opened stays unlocked and open after Seyda Neen and back and after a quicksave and quickload; a Seyda Neen door locked at 75 stays locked at 75 after another map and a load; two items taken from Elone stay marked stolen from her after another map and a load. Container contents fixed in v0.0.59 (third slice): what is taken out of or put into a placed container is kept per container as the difference against its game-data contents, on the same list, kept for the session and saved; taking from an owned container is theft; a script's AddItem, RemoveItem and GetItemCount on a container use the same entries. Verified at 32 MB Fast on a Seyda Neen MiniWind: 4 of the 10 gold taken from the owned Small Chest in Arrille's Tradehouse stay taken after Seyda Neen and back and after a quicksave and quickload; an iron dagger put into the same chest stays there the same way. Still open: no in-game action moves an object yet (the field is saved and read by the placed items), no container window yet (the console's aw_placed container takes and puts), respawning containers and levelled lists inside containers, and the later slices of CELL-CHANGES-59.

title: The Solstheim test frame converts its trees as full models, not through the world flora cards Vvardenfell uses
status: Open: the expansions have no path through the island's build pipeline. The --dlc and --no-dlc options only record the chosen layers; the one expansion path is the test-only Solstheim stage, which runs the CHIM world step alone on chosen cells: none of the world terrain, scenery, flora card, harvest, room, resident or NPC stages, and none of their reductions. So every Bloodmoon tree went in as its full model (472 to 724 faces) and the views drew 45,964 faces at the median against 7,562 on Vvardenfell: not a like-for-like comparison. Fix: each layer is built by the same stages as Vvardenfell, exteriors and interiors, with every optimization, keyed by the layer's own files; then measured again.
where: tools/build.py chim-sol stage (tools/chim_build.py without --flora)
severity_reason: The published Solstheim face figures compare full tree models with Vvardenfell's tree cards

status: Seen on the second v0.0.66-dev1 build: "Morrowind.esm: reference number 4201598 does not fit 20 bits". The merged master gives an expansion's reference the key game master index x 2^22 + its own number (4201598 = Tribunal's reference 7294), and the stages hand it to the stable id as a number of the base game. Fix: the stable id reads such a key as the reference of the master it names, in the same fixed order of the game files; a test pins it with that number.

reports.note: Seen again in play of v0.0.67-dev1, in a Tribunal Dwemer ruin: the creature was there but none of the containers tried would open. Another possible cause is locked containers without a key (LOCKED-CONTAINERS-NEVER-OPEN-67).

Seen again in the engine (the container count on the v0.0.66 release build): the room records of the expansions' rooms name each placement by the merged master's number (master index x 2^22 + its own number), the use table by the stable id (master index x 2^20 + number), and the engine compares the two as they are (chim_room.c ChimRoom_Has, ChimRoom_RayRef, ChimRoom_Hide). In the 150 built rooms of Tribunal and Bloodmoon a placed item therefore counts as not drawn and cannot be taken, a taken one is not hidden, and 1,709 containers are aimed by their measured box only.

Seen again in the trap table of the v0.0.67-dev2 build: the trapped containers of the expansions (Tribunal 2, Bloodmoon 6; the first, the Ornate Dwemer Chest (dwrv_chest_satchel00) in Bamz-Amschend, Hall of Winds) have their trap rows under the merged master's number (tools/prepare_door_audio.py trap_catalogue), while the engine looks a container's trap up by its use-table reference, the stable id (aw_inventory.c container_open, aw_hinged_door.c trap_row), so these traps never spring. The doors' trap, lock and door rows use the merged number on both sides and are not affected.

Seen again in the jail's markers of the v0.0.67-dev2 build (id1/prison-markers.txt, tools/world_doors.py prison_markers): the evidence chests of Mournhold, Royal Palace: Jail (4217167) and Fort Frostmoth, Prison (8420587) are written under the merged master's number, while the engine changes a container's contents under its use-table reference, the stable id (aw_crime.c confiscate, AW_ContainerChange), so the stolen things an arrest takes there go to a container nobody opens. status: Closed: fixed in source (afa819f4, gate 10650), shipped in v0.0.66-dev2, confirmed by that build, whose world survey passed with both expansions selected. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev2: the survey reads the archives of the selected masters and plans the base game exterior grid, including the expansions edits to it. Exterior cells that only an expansion adds (155 Solstheim cells) are listed in the survey as expansion_only_cells and are not planned until that exterior is converted; planning them would renumber the vf maps and the recorded refinements. title: A save is written as good although the changed actors or script values failed to go into it
status: Open: fixed in source (4b32d948, gate 10210; its follow-ups in v0.0.66-dev3) and shipped in v0.0.66-dev2; awaiting confirmation: in play on a numbered build, a save whose part cannot be kept is refused with the line naming the part and the previous save unchanged (the opening journey's quicksave shows saves still work, not a refusal). title: A saved script's values are matched to the compiled script only by its row: a rebuild in another order drops them
status: Open: fixed in source (a3d8708f, gate 10211) and shipped in v0.0.66-dev2; awaiting confirmation: a save made on one numbered build loaded on a later one whose scripts were rebuilt in another order, with its script values back by name. Before: The fix: a saved script is found by its name (the saved row only tried first; a rebuilt file finds a moved script with one read of every row's name hash), and every saved script value now carries its variable's name and type, with a signature of the script's variables. While a script's variables are as saved, values go back by their slot; when a rebuild inserted, removed, reordered or retyped them, each value goes to the variable of its name (converted between whole numbers and floats as the original engine does); a value whose variable is gone is left out and counted, and the load says so in one line. Two names that share a hash are never mixed: the builder refuses such script, global and quest names, and two variables of one script that share one are restored only while the script is unchanged. Older saves load by slot as before.

history.note: Cause found. The build holds every outdoor creature: the v0.0.66 release build's actor table has all 329 placed creatures and 4,974 levelled points of the region cells and the 4 and 112 of the town cells, each with a model, and the town join of v0.0.66-dev2 spawns Seyda Neen's (53 creatures queued and alive in the release's delivery smoke). The game loses them in two places. (1) The server sends the entity updates in edict order and stops when the datagram is full; the creatures the cells join are spawned last, the highest edicts, so every frame that overflows leaves them out first (NET-VIVEC-ENTITY-PACKET-OVERFLOW-66; the overflow is printed in the wild in v0.0.66). (2) The cell the player arrives in never gets its levelled creatures (OUTDOOR-CREATURES-HOME-CELL-67), about nine in ten of the wild's creatures. The image step's actor spec check passed because it counted the table's rows, not what the engine can spawn (BUILD-ACTOR-SPEC-UNSPAWNABLE-67).

When it changed, from the delivery hops of every version (the same teleports each time): the region frames of v0.0.62, v0.0.65 and v0.0.66-dev1 join the same three cells around the arrival with the same counts (by Ald'ruhn -3 6, -3 7, -2 7; by Khuul -9 16, -8 16, -8 17), never the arrival cell, and no frame overflows: nothing changed in the region joins or the entity sending between v0.0.62 and v0.0.65 (the v0.0.65 report was the town cells of Seyda Neen). v0.0.66-dev2 added the town join (Vivec queues 85 creatures). From v0.0.66-dev3 the entity update overflows (732 lines in Vivec, none in dev2; about 2,100 a stay since), and in v0.0.66 it reached the wild, where it drops the joined creatures first.
Seen again in play on the v0.0.66 release on 17 November: no wildlife outdoors.

title: With the expansions selected the build stopped at the focus table: activators and containers of Tribunal and Bloodmoon had no measured box, and their rooms had no rows
status: Closed: fixed in source (d6abf612, gate 10611), shipped in v0.0.66-dev2, confirmed by that build, whose focus stage passed with both expansions selected. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev2. Cause: the focus table's measured boxes of named activators (FOCUS_BOXES) and containers (CONTAINER_BOXES) in tools/prepare_focus.py were measured from the base game's models only; the first build with Tribunal and Bloodmoon selected (v0.0.66-dev2, commit ef8b9700) stopped 13 s into its focus stage on a Bloodmoon activator (act_bm_stone_beast_01) without a box. With both expansions selected, 41 activator models and 23 container models had no box. Besides, the tables keyed by room number (the focus table, the placed item list, the per-area tables) took only the base game's rooms, so the expansions' 194 interiors (Mournhold, Solstheim) got no rows, and the actor stats' levelled lists per area read the base game file alone. Fix: the 64 models measured the same way from the expansion archives and added; the room numbers of every selected master; a build preflight (and the plan check) that names every placed, named activator or container of the selected masters without a box, in seconds, before any stage. With the base game alone the outputs do not change, except 69 placed Raw Ebony rocks of the base game, whose models are now measured (for the Raven Rock colony's ebony rocks) and which therefore carry their aim box too. Still base-only by design and listed, not changed here: the harvest catalogue (the base game's mushrooms), the dialogue table, the exterior plan's source cells (EXPANSION-TABLES-BASE-ONLY-66). Checked by tests and the gate; not yet seen in play. The stages that read the merged master with the base archive alone are EXPANSION-ARCHIVE-READERS-66.

The save must hold every change the game makes, with no fixed cap that can refuse a save or silently drop state.

status: Closed: fixed in source (b7991981 and 62f6b990, gate 10813), shipped in v0.0.66-dev3 (the first build that holds them; the entry named v0.0.66-dev2), confirmed by that build's pre-flight, run on 24 worker processes with the source analysis taken from its check. Fixed and measured. The pre-flight before the first stage runs on a process pool of --jobs workers, capped by the cores the build may use, and its stage source analysis is worked out once per source tree. (1) The cache owner check (tools/build_preflight.py) walked every entry of the workspace cache on one core, about 14 million entries and a third of the check; it now hands the subtrees to the pool and joins the results in the walk's own order, with the same message. (2) The stage source analysis (tools/fingerprint_prefetch.py) reads every Python module of the checkout once on the pool, then works out each stage script in forked workers; the entry check's reuse preflight and the stage plan share it. (3) The analysis is kept in WORKSPACE/cache/preflight-analysis-v1, keyed by the SHA-256 of every file it covers, the checkout folder, the key form and the analysing code, and the next check or build of the same tree takes it; the log says which (Pre-flight: stage source analysis computed / taken from the check of TIME). Build options and environment switches still count in the stage keys themselves. Measured on the v0.0.66-dev2 inputs of 1cbb84c (the same check command, environment and reuse source, 8-core containers beside other work, the change alone between the two trees): the check took 672.6 s before and 153.0 s with the change (the cache check 13.4 s, the stage source analysis 9.1 s for 48 stage scripts and 590 modules); a second check of the same tree took the kept analysis in under 2 s (166.6 s in all, beside a starting build). Every one of the 43 reused stages had the same fingerprint before and after.

title: The census office's two scripted doors of the captain's wing open only once: used a second time, E does nothing (the exit door to Seyda Neen, and the courtyard door into his room)
status: Closed: fixed in source (baf85a6c, gate 10870), shipped in v0.0.66-dev4, confirmed in play by the opening journey's step 6 on v0.0.66-dev5 and every journey since. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev4 (baf85a6c) and seen in play on the v0.0.66-dev4 image (2026_11_15_v0.0.66-dev4_full-v0.0.66-dev4_010ce4a, FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast, JIT): in the opening journey's second run on that image, after the release the player went back into Sellus Gravius' room by the street door (113833), left by the courtyard door (119660), came in again from the courtyard (113889) and left by the exit door (119659) to the street; every door opened, and all four checks of the journey's step 6 passed. Before: Played twice on the v0.0.66-dev2 image (the opening journey, part A). Run journey4: the exit door (119659, "CharGen Exit Door", script CharGenDoorExitCaptain) let the player out at the release; back in Sellus Gravius' room by the street door (113833), E on the same exit door did nothing (no load, no message). Run journey8: the courtyard door into his room (113889, "chargen door captain", script CharGenDoorEnterCaptain) opened in step 4; in step 6 the player came in by the street door, left by the room's other courtyard door (119660, no script: it opened) and, back in the courtyard, E on 113889 again did nothing although the game's use focus was on it. Doors without a script opened again (the back-room door 119665 twice). Cause: both scripts keep a local done. On the use that opens the door they set it to 1 and call Activate; from then on they return at their first lines, before OnActivate, so they never read OnActivate again. In the original, as OpenMW 0.51 keeps the rule (mwworld/refdata.cpp: onActivate, activateByScript, activate), a script takes the player's use only while it reads OnActivate; its own Activate gives the use back to the object, so after done the doors open as plain doors. The engine took the use of every object whose script contains OnActivate at all (aw_mwhost.c object_intercept), and the script never read it again: the use was lost, every time, also after the player left and came back (done is kept with the door). Fix, for v0.0.66 (after the v0.0.66-dev3 snapshot's build): the interpreter keeps the rule per object (aw_mwvm.c: OnActivate marks the next use as the script's, the object's Activate clears it, AW_MwvmUse answers whether a use is the script's); the engine's door, item, actor and console uses ask it. Every scripted object follows it, not only these two doors. Native tests: tests/test_mwscript.py ScriptedUseTests (a door refused, opened once, then plain also after the room is left and entered again; a door whose script keeps reading OnActivate keeps the use). Waiting for a build to check it in the game. Also recorded from the opening journey's runs (the journey on foot, tests/sessions/journey_opening.txt; its branch had filed the same bug under this ID, folded in here): in run journey4, back in the room by the street door, the crosshair's pick named the exit door (source ref 119659) before E did nothing, and the game's aim report there read 381 rows, the town's focus table, where the first visit from the courtyard read the room's 154 rows (not looked at apart from the doors); in run journey8 the use focus on 113889 was the aw_placed aim's row 173. The journey's step 6 now checks the fix in the game: after the release it goes back in by the street door (113833), leaves by the courtyard door (119660), comes in again from the courtyard (113889) and leaves by the exit door (119659); a stop at either door names which one.

title: The gameplay journey lost its way in the census office: its key presses talked to the clerk and chose Persuasion instead of taking the papers, and every later step ran in that window
status: Closed: fixed in source (3d63acef, gate 10870), shipped in v0.0.66-dev4 (the first build that holds it; the entry named v0.0.66-dev3), confirmed by the opening journey's full pass on v0.0.66-dev7. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev4 (3d63acef, with later steps of the walk refined in the same line). Before: On the v0.0.66-dev2 image the opening journey reported 19 of 33 checks failed. Its walk pressed the use key after walking up to the clerk, which opens his dialogue window, not the papers on the table; the Enter that followed picked the first row of his topic list, which is always Persuasion. The window stayed open, so the papers were never taken and the later steps (Sellus Gravius, the take, the kill, the spell) pressed their keys into it. Two more faults of the walk: Sellus Gravius stands in the other wing of the office, reached only through the hall door, the back room, the courtyard and the captain's door, so a straight walk toward him from the clerk's room cannot reach him; and the walk played this part with key counts that had never been run on an image (the v0.0.65 opening walk it came from added the papers with a console command and opened his window with a debug command). The fix, in the journey tools: the walk waits for the game and stops at the first wrong turn (walk to a point until the engine says it is there, wait for a window or a map, answer message boxes, aim at a named reference and check what the crosshair is on, choose a dialogue topic by its name in the window's search box), and the journey walks the real route through the office.

title: In the opening, fighting is already switched on before the release papers are taken; the original keeps it off from the ship until the papers
status: Closed: fixed in source (48f95e12, gate 10881), shipped in v0.0.66-dev5, confirmed in play by the opening journey's step 1 on that build. Seen fixed in play on the v0.0.66-dev5 image (FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast, JIT): the opening journey's first step passes all six of its checks: on the ship and before the papers are taken the fighting switch reads on (1 and 1, both 0 on the v0.0.66-dev4 image), the papers are not taken before and taken after the census office (0, then 1), and after the papers fighting and magic read off (0 and 0). Fixed in v0.0.66-dev5 (48f95e12). Before: Played on the v0.0.66-dev2 image (five sessions, the journey and the dev2 chain's journey): on the prison ship about ten seconds after New Game, and again right after the clerk's stat review, before the papers are taken, aw_mwscript_status call getplayerfightingdisabled reads 0 and the control switch mask is 0, so every switch is on from the start. In the original the CharGen script switches fighting off at the start (DisablePlayerFighting, with jumping, magic and the view switch) and the papers' own script CharGenStatsSheet, the hall guard and the courtyard barrel switch it on again (docs/CHARACTER_CREATION.md; the opening sequence notes). Cause: CharGen is one of the opening scripts AmiWind carries with its own code (config/mwscript.json handwritten). Its counterpart (engine/aga/src/aw_story.c AW_StoryReset, with the NGWE weather row) set CharGenState 10 and the weather from the script but left out its six control switches (DisablePlayerControls, -Jumping, -ViewSwitch, VanityMode, -Fighting, -Magic), and the New Game reset clears every switch, as OpenMW's does, so every switch read on from the start. The opening's own rule (AW_StoryFighting) still kept the attack and the weapon down until the papers, but the scripts' switches, which the census scripts that run switch on again (the clerk, the papers, the hall guard, the courtyard barrel, the exit door), read on throughout, and no input honoured DisablePlayerMagic at all (the ready-magic key readied magic before the papers). Fixed in source (for v0.0.66-dev5, branch v0.0.66-openingfix): the compiler writes the switches each carried new-game script sets on its first run as NGCS rows of id1/mwscript.awm (tools/mwscript/gamedata.py new_game_controls, awms.py new_game_control_rows); the engine sets them at the new game's first script tick, only while the opening is at its start on the ship (aw_mwhost.c new_game_controls, aw_story.c AW_StoryNewGameControls; not for a quick start, a demo, a debug scene on the pier or the census type legacy path). The hand-carried CharGenWalkNPC switches the controls on after its movement box and CharGenRaceNPC off at its greeting and on at its state 50, as the original scripts do (aw_intro.c, aw_opening.c); the ready-magic key does not ready magic while a script has the magic or the controls switched off (aw_cast.c, as OpenMW 0.51 playercontrols.lua ToggleSpell). The build refuses a script file in which a switch the new game turns off is switched on again by no script it runs (tools/mwscript/newgame.py check). Every script that switches a control off goes through the same switches. Tests: tests/test_mwscript_new_game.py NewGameControlsTests, tests/aga_controls_test.c. The opening journey's walk from the town's start point to the pier also passed within 400 units of the courtyard barrel, whose script switches fighting, magic and jumping on (its map box came up on the pier), so its fight_before probe would read 0 for that reason as well; the journey now walks round it (tests/sessions/journey_opening.txt).

title: Census back room: looking at the crab meat on the table, the use key goes to the silver plate under it, so E steals the plate instead of taking the crab meat
status: Closed: fixed in source (d7dd7443, gate 10881), shipped in v0.0.66-dev5, confirmed in play by the opening journey's step 2 on v0.0.66-dev6 and every journey since. Seen fixed in play on the v0.0.66-dev6 image (FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast, JIT) (the game is that of v0.0.66-dev5): the opening journey's part A, step 2, passes "crab_before == 0", "crab_after == 1" and "lacks plate_ledger misc_imp_silverware_plate_01": the use key took the crab meat (`ingred_crab_meat_01`) and the Silverware Plate under it was not taken. Played on the v0.0.66-dev2 image (the opening journey, part A): standing at the back-room table's edge and looking down at the crab meat (reference 454283), the crosshair's collision pick names the crab meat, but the game's use focus (aw_placed aim: aimed row 43) is the Silverware Plate (119580) it lies on, at almost the same centre. E took the plate (its row then reads disabled 1; the plate belongs to a shady smuggler, so the take is a theft) and the crab meat count stayed 0; after it the crab meat is focused and shows E: Take. In the original the use goes to the object the view ray meets first, the crab meat on top. Two items with nearly the same centre are told apart by the distance from the view ray alone. The v0.0.58 census tray smoke took the crab meat first from another spot. Cause (engine/aga/src/aw_inventory.c placed_target): the census office is a compiled room whose small items are edicts of their own (brush entities that carry their reference), and the rows the map draws itself were aimed by the near-the-origin test alone: of the rows within 4 map units of the crosshair line the one whose origin lay nearest along the view won. The crab meat (454283, at 580.7 704.1 251.0 in the original units) lies on the plate (119580, at 580.2 704.1 251.1), both passed, and the plate's origin, a fraction of a unit nearer, took the use: of two items lying one on the other the winner was decided by their origins, never by what the view meets. Fixed in source (for v0.0.66-dev5, branch v0.0.66-openingfix, commit d7dd7443): the use goes to what the view ray meets first, as the original and OpenMW 0.51 test the activation ray against the objects. One point trace along the reach a call (view_reference): an item drawn as an edict of its own that the trace meets is aimed at that point, wherever the ray lands on it; an item a CHIM room draws is ranked by where the ray enters its placement box (ChimRoom_RayRef, as a room's container already was); a placed-list item by its model, as before. Every item lying on another follows the rule wherever it is drawn as an edict or by a CHIM room; an item a CHIM frame draws outdoors keeps the origin test. aw_placed aim now prints what the view ray meets first and always lists the aimed row (the crab meat's row was past the first twelve the report printed). Tests: tests/aga_focus_pickup_test.c (the plate and the crab meat half a unit apart: the ray on the crab meat takes the crab meat, on the plate's rim the plate, with the view turned 20 degrees off both origins the crab meat where the ray meets it), tests/test_activate.py.

title: Coming back out of the census office onto the Seyda Neen street after a kill, the player arrives inside the guard who has walked to the door and stays stuck
status: Fixed in source, covered by tests, to be confirmed in play (branch v0.0.66-doorarrival). Cause: outdoors the scene's actors join after the arrival's check: they are queued with the arrival's ring, spawned over the next ticks and then moved to where the saved changes left them. The guard (reference 128967), who walks by his Wander package, had walked to the street door while the player was inside (WANDER-DOOR-RULE-66; in the dev6 journey he already stood in front of that door before step 6; no crime was involved: the journey's console kill is not counted as the player's crime and nobody pursued), and came back 8 units from the arrival point, his box overlapping the player's by 6.2 units across. Quake's box clip then held both: a sweep that starts inside the sum of two boxes is solid until one frame's move leaves it whole and the walk zeroes the velocity, and the stuck search, which counted every body, failed in every frame ("player is stuck.", up to 164 position tests each time). A player could not walk out: in the native test at the measured boxes and positions, ten frames of walking away moved the player 0 units. The fix, for every door, teleport and actor: two bodies that already overlap collide as the original game's actors do (OpenMW 0.51 actorconvexcallback.cpp): only a move toward the other's centre stops, so they walk apart (engine/aga/src/world.c AW_BodyOverlap, aw_body_overlap 1); the stuck search leaves other bodies out (SV_TestWorldPosition); and for three seconds after an arrival an actor that joins onto the player steps the player once to the nearest clear standing spot beside the point (aw_scene.c, aw_arrival_clear 1, the console line "Arrival: ... stood on the arrival point"). Both are on in id1/default-game.cfg; 0 gives the old behaviour back. Tests: tests/aga_body_overlap_test.c (walking away: 30 units in ten frames, no stuck search) and the arrival case in tests/aga_scene_test.c. The next opening journey should print that Arrival line after step 6's return (or none, if the guard stands elsewhere) and no "player is stuck." lines. The v0.0.66-dev9 journey did not exercise the case: with the victim fixed in the west of the town, no actor stood on the street door's arrival point after step 6 (no "Arrival:" line) and the console of neither part has a "player is stuck." line, so the fix has not been seen at work and the entry stays open.

title: The build's reuse check runs about six minutes on one core, and every snapshot runs it twice before its build starts
status: Closed: fixed in source (7e502993, gate 10941), shipped in v0.0.66-dev11, confirmed by that build, which took its starter's passed check instead of running it again. Confirmed on the v0.0.66-dev11 build (26ed570f, 16 November 2026): the build request took the passed check of the identical starter request (the same commit, earlier build, flags, check command and runs in the workspace, 58 seconds old) instead of running it again; the build log says the check was taken and not run again. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev11. Before: Measured on the v0.0.66-dev7 and v0.0.66-dev8 snapshots: the reuse check of the snapshot's commit (the build's --check, the stage plan and the reuse stop) ran 5 to 6 minutes before the build was asked for (dev7 17:41 to 17:47, dev8 19:58 to 20:04, 15 November 2026), and the build then ran its own check of the same commit against the same earlier build before any stage started, another 7 minutes (dev7 17:47:42 to 17:54:41, dev8 20:05:04 to 20:12:18); dev9 and dev10 the same. Cause, from a profile of the check on the v0.0.66-dev10 inputs (commit f446092 against the dev9 build, 46 of 48 stages reused, 16 November 2026): the second check is the first one again (the same command, commit, earlier build and flags), and the check itself waits on the disk more than on the cores. Run alone with the build's own settings it took 332.1 s with the check's 4 workers and 341.4 s with every core the build may use: the cache owner walk (14.2 million entries) 142.6 s (116.0 s with every core), the plan's SHA-256 check of the 116,024 files (14.6 GiB) the build takes from the earlier build 93 s (73 s with every core, on 8 threads), the plans of the 7 other earlier builds of the workspace one after another 22.5 s (81 s with every core), the unit-cache report 13 s (its key digests one after another), the developer-mode reuse preflight 17 s, the game files 17.6 s and the grounding checks 18.5 s. Fix: a build request takes the passed check of an identical earlier request (the same full commit, earlier build, build flags, check command and runs in the workspace, at most 30 minutes old, tools/aw_service.py), so a snapshot runs the check once; the plan's SHA-256 check runs on as many threads as the build may use cores (at least 8, at most 32) and the unit-cache keys on the pre-flight's worker processes. After, the same check of the fixed builder (63259004) with every core the build may use: the plan's SHA-256 check 64.7 s on one thread per core (73.4 s on 8 before), the unit-cache report 3.9 s with its 12 cache keys on 12 worker processes (11.5 s before), the whole check 298.8 s against 341.4 s (single runs; the parts that read the disk vary by up to a third from run to run, and this was the first check of the new builder, which works out the stored source analyses again once). The larger saving is the second check: the build request takes the first one's result instead of running it again, which took 4.5 to 8.2 minutes on the dev7 to dev10 snapshots. Fixed in source, to be confirmed by the next snapshot's chain.
