title: In Vivec the server's entity update overflows the client datagram every frame: packet overflow printed 1,938 times during one 45-second stay
status: Open. Seen in the v0.0.66-dev7 delivery's area hops (FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast, JIT): all 1,938 packet overflow lines of the session fall between the Vivec load and the next teleport (lines 315 to 2252 of the console), none in Seyda Neen, Balmora, the arena pit, Ald'ruhn or Khuul; the passing rerun printed them as well. Next: count the entities Vivec sends a frame against the datagram size, and decide between a larger datagram, fewer sent entities (distance or visibility), or a quieter line.
where: engine/aga/src/sv_main.c SV_WriteEntitiesToClient; maps/vivec_city-chim.chim (the delivery's area hops console)
severity_reason: in a full frame the message ran past its buffer and the game stopped on the loading screen (the v0.0.66 release, outdoors); the highest entity numbers, the joined creatures and residents, were left out of every full frame

reports.note: Seen in the v0.0.66 release outdoors, by the maintainer: the Bitter Coast, cell -2,-8 (global -13677 -61720 604), no door used; about 30 "packet overflow" lines, then "SZ_GetSpace: overflow" and "CL_ParseServerMessage: Illegible server message"; the loading screen stayed up and the music played on. The game stopped, not only a missed update.

platform: FS-UAE 3.1.66, JIT, A1200 68040 preset, 32 MB Fast

history.note: Cause found on 17 November 2026 (v0.0.67 line, from the engine source and the stop the maintainer met in the v0.0.66 release on the Bitter Coast, cell -2,-8, about 30 "packet overflow" lines, then "SZ_GetSpace: overflow" and "CL_ParseServerMessage: Illegible server message", the loading screen left up, the music playing on). Every frame the game's server writes the updates of everything in sight into one message of 1024 bytes for its screen side, in entity order, and stopped ("packet overflow") once fewer than 16 bytes were left. An update has taken up to 21 bytes since the 3-byte coordinates of v0.0.36 (CHIM-FRAME-COORD-RANGE-33), 22 since the 2-byte model number of v0.0.59-dev4 (ENGINE-MODEL-TABLE-58); the AmiWind fields of v0.0.52 (a scale, a frame over 255) were reserved on top. So the last update could run up to 6 bytes past the buffer. That buffer's overflow flag was never set (a stack buffer whose allowoverflow held whatever was there): the message was cleared and written on from the middle of an update, and the screen side stopped on it. In every full frame the highest entity numbers were left out, the creatures and residents a town joins last (the missing wildlife of OUTDOOR-CREATURES-REGRESSION-66). When it started: the short reserve since v0.0.36; full frames where many things are in sight at once, first registered in Vivec in v0.0.66-dev7 and outdoors in the v0.0.66 release. Fixed in source on the v0.0.67 line: every update built whole first and copied in only where it fits, the player, the actors and the nearest first, the rest in the next frames (none waits for good); the game's own connection carries 8 KB; every message buffer allows its overflow explicitly and a message that still overflows is dropped whole and said once; the screen side drops a frame update it cannot read instead of ending the game; an error in play loads the place again with the box (docs/NET_MESSAGES.md).

A second console picture of the same error was sent: the game breaks with the overflow lines and the Host_Error. No delivery check walked the open world or failed on these lines: CHECKS-NO-WILD-WALK-67.

Seen outdoors on the v0.0.66 release, walking away from a tree in the Bitter Coast region (cell -2,-8, local about -603 2489 151) with no door or travel: the loading screen showed and stayed. The console then showed about thirty lines of packet overflow, then SZ_GetSpace: overflow and Host_Error: CL_ParseServerMessage: Illegible server message; the music kept playing. The load stops on that Host_Error, so the stuck loading screen is this overflow ending in an error, no longer only a message. Not seen in earlier versions. The load fallback work of the v0.0.67-dev2 line (gate 11151) adds a 120 second load time limit with an OK box and the way back, which would end such a hang; the cause, the frame streamed at that spot, is still to be found.

Follow-up on the v0.0.67 line (17 November 2026): on the game's own connection the frame message's room is no longer fixed. It starts at 32768 bytes (aw_net_frame), the screen side's receive buffer at 65536 (aw_net_buffer), both allocated; a frame that wants more than three quarters of the room doubles it for the next frame, never in the middle of a message and never past 262144 bytes (aw_net_max), with one console line per growth; nothing shrinks while a map runs; the length of a message on that connection is three bytes. Two methods, switched live with aw_net_method and saved: 1 FULL (every update in sight each frame, the room growing) and 2 PACED (at most aw_net_send bytes a frame, 4096 at the start, the actors and the nearest first, the rest in the next frames). FULL is the default until the in-game comparison (docs/performance/NET_FRAME.md, session tests/sessions/net_frame_methods.txt). dbg netstat names the method, its budget, the room and its growth, the fullest frame and its share of the room, the waits, the frame time and the screen side's reading time; dbg netstat reset starts a new measuring window. A reliable message stays at most 16380 bytes. The "before" line, the v0.0.67-dev1 engine in the game: 4668 "packet overflow" console lines at Vivec from the arrival on, none at the wilderness spot of the v0.0.66 stop in that run.

title: A wandering resident can stop at a destination right by a door and stand there; the original sends an idle wanderer near a door walking
status: REGRESSED in v0.0.66-dev12 (fixed in v0.0.66-dev11 before): The v0.0.66-dev12 opening journey (ac37e80b) stopped part B in step 9 as the dev10 journey had: the use key aimed at the door 113833 went to the actor Fargoth standing in front of it (focus row 164) in 13 tries around pitch 9.9 and yaw 264.5; the dev11 journey had passed once. One passing run does not confirm a fix that depends on where actors walk.. Before: Closed: fixed in source (237b5a6f, gate 10941), shipped in v0.0.66-dev11, confirmed in play by the opening journey's step 9 on that build. Confirmed in play on v0.0.66-dev11 (26ed570f, gate 10941): the opening journey passed 42 of 42 checks, and its step 9 went through the Census and Excise Office's street door (113833) in Seyda Neen with no resident in the way (on dev10 the aim at that door went to Fargoth, `fargoth`, in 12 of 13 tries). Fixed in v0.0.66-dev11. Before: Fixed in source, covered by tests, to be confirmed by the next opening journey. Cause: the residents' Wander packages (engine/aga/src/aw_ambient.c) had no door rule, so a wanderer whose destination lay right by a door stood there through its idles, in front of the door and on its arrival point. The original sends such a wanderer on: OpenMW 0.51 checks an idle wanderer every 1.5 seconds and sends it walking when it faces a door within 1.6 times the activation distance (aiwander.cpp onIdleStatePerFrameActions; obstacle.cpp proximityToDoor: at most 60 degrees off its facing, heights left out, only a door that is shut and still), and a walker that has to evade with a door within the activation distance drops that destination and the allowed ones on its path and takes another (aiwander.cpp evadeObstacles, trimAllowedPositions). Seen: in the v0.0.66-dev6 and dev7 opening journeys the guard (reference 128967) stood by the street door of the Census and Excise Office (113833) in Seyda Neen; in the v0.0.66-dev10 journey Fargoth (fargoth, 128964) stood 55 units from that door's reference and 12 of the 13 aims at the door in step 9 went to him. The fix, for every wanderer and every door: both checks in aw_ambient.c, against the place's load doors at their references' positions (the focus table's door rows, aw_inventory.c AW_PlacedDoors) and the map's hinged doors that stand shut and still (aw_hinged_door.c AW_HingedDoorShut); a disabled door never counts; a resident with wander distance 0, or one that only walks to spots near its start, stays as before. "chim actors ambient doors on" is the default in id1/default-game.cfg; "chim actors ambient doors off" gives the old behaviour back; "chim actors ambient" prints the checks. Tests: tests/aga_ambient_test.c (a door ahead within the distance and 60 degrees; facing away or farther stays idle; no check without a distance or routes; a stuck walker drops its destination and those on its route and never picks them again) and tests/test_ambient_lut.py. The next opening journey should show step 9 aimed at the street door with no resident named by the aim, and the doors line of "chim actors ambient" with idle residents sent on.

Cause of the return in the v0.0.67-dev2 opening journey (part B, step 9, after the game's own quicksave was loaded) found: a Wander package's compiled route points are offsets from the actor's placement, but the engine added them to where the actor stood when its package started (aw_ambient.c start). After a loaded game that is the saved spot, so every destination lay off the path grid by the saved offset. Fargoth (128964, placed at 188 115 in the Seyda Neen frame) stood after the load at 228 62 (his row from the save), beside his grid destination by the Census and Excise Office's street door (245 63; the door 113833 at 247 11), so his routes lay 40 units east and 53 south of the game data's, and he stayed there through all 13 aims at the door. He was joined once (69 actors alive, as before the load). The original keeps the package's start in the saved game (OpenMW 0.51 aiwander.cpp mInitialActorPosition, written and read with the package) and takes the allowed position nearest the actor as its current one. Fix: the actor spawner tells the package where each actor was placed before a saved row moves it (aw_actors.c SpawnOne and ApplyLoaded, aw_ambient.c AW_AmbientPlacedAt), the routes stay there, and the current destination is the allowed one nearest the actor; tests/aga_ambient_test.c holds Fargoth's compiled package as the v0.0.67-dev2 build has it and fails with the old rule.

A session from the v0.0.67-dev2 journey's quicksave on that image's own engine (the rule before 3e7308b9; FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast, warp off): Fargoth stood at 228.7 62.5 for the whole 90 seconds. His Wander slot was made after the save's changes had moved him there (the console's "the save's changes applied to 17 of the scene's actors" comes before the frames in which the residents' slots were made and their combat facts read), so the old rule started his routes at that spot, 40.4 units east and 53.0 south of his placement (that engine prints no route start; the fixed one does). His first walk, to his destination 4 by way of 1 (the grid point by the street door), failed against the player standing beside him, and he stayed in his idles; the idle door check never found the door ahead (0 of 223 checks: he did not face it). From the street door's arrival point the use key went to him in 5 of 8 aims and to a passing guard in 2 before the door opened (see FOCUS-NPC-OVERRIDES-ITEM-62 for why from 37 units).

The same session with the fixed engine (gate 11462 on d9556d22): the use key went to the street door on the 4th aim from its arrival point, no actor in the way (aims 1 to 3 had the door 6.0 to 6.7 units off the aim). Its counters: of the 17 residents the save's rows moved, 11 had their Wander slot already (made at their placement, before the move) and 6 got it after; the routes stayed at the placement in both cases. Fargoth was one of the 11: the row put him at his saved spot, 270 168, where his current destination became the nearest one (his grid point there, 11 to 15 units off, inside the arrival distance of 16), and he played his idles there (state idle, no waypoint) through all 9 lists, about 160 units from the door; the goal it lists (0) is left from the walk he had begun at his placement before the move, which the move ended. This corrects the reading of the session on the old engine: there his slot was most likely made before the move too, so his routes started at his placement; what held him by the door was that walk, begun at the placement toward his destination 4 by way of the grid point by the door (245 63), which the old rule let go on from the saved spot after the move until the player standing on that point stopped him at 228 62. The route start taken from the saved spot was the case of the slots made after the move. Both are fixed by the same change. The fixed engine's first version listed his route start as 185 112 44, not his placement 188.30 115.46 42.15: it took the spot where his walk had brought him when the row moved him (4.7 units toward destination 0); not a grounding difference, corrected after gate 11462 (the start of a slot made before the move is kept).

title: The opening journey's step 7 fights the nearest resident, which can be Fargoth, who fights unarmed, so the health may stay as it was
status: Closed: fixed in source (c2aef5f3, gate 10941), shipped in v0.0.66-dev11, confirmed by the opening journey's step 7 on that build. Confirmed on v0.0.66-dev11 (26ed570f, gate 10941): the opening journey passed 42 of 42 checks; its step 7 cast and fought a fighter named by reference (the check "has fighter ref" passed), and the health after the fight was below the health after the heal. Fixed in v0.0.66-dev11. Before: Fixed in source, covered by tests, to be confirmed by the next journey (commit c2aef5f3). Seen in the opening journey on the v0.0.66-dev9 and dev10 images: step 7 copied the nearest resident as the fighter, which was Fargoth (`fargoth`), who fights unarmed (misses and fatigue damage only; hand-to-hand hurts the fatigue first, as in the original), so the check "health_fought < health_healed" failed by chance; on the dev7 image another resident was nearest and the step passed. The fix: "chim actors summon" takes an optional reference (the record's reference number, as "chim actors kill" does) and copies the living resident of that reference to the player's feet (engine/aga/src/aw_actors.c); without a reference it still copies the nearest resident, and a reference of nobody living there copies nobody and prints "no living actor of reference N here". Step 7 now summons the Seyda Neen guard (128967), who carries a weapon, by reference, as step 6 names its victim; every other step is as it was. Tests: the engine actor test (tests/aga_actors_test.c, mode summonref, run by tests/test_aw_actors_native.py: the bare form, the farthest resident by reference, an unknown and a dead reference) and tests/test_journey_smoke.py (step 7 names the guard, the one summon line of the journey, a fight that lands no hit still fails step 7). The next journey's step 7 should print "chim actors summon: a copy of Guard (ref 900500)" and the fight line should name the copy, with the health after the fight below the health after the heal; if it prints "no living actor of reference 128967 here" the guard is not in the loaded area at that point and the step needs another armed resident.

title: A script's read or write of another object's local variable finds nothing: the engine takes the object row's id as its script, so the read gives 0 and the write is dropped (Dagoth Ur's shield never follows the Heart's count)
status: Closed: fixed in source (7024bf28, gate 10941), shipped in v0.0.66-dev11, confirmed in play by the end of the main quest session on that build. Confirmed in play on v0.0.66-dev11 (26ed570f, run 3 of the end of the main quest session, the emulator's deterministic option on, FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast): after each of the first three strikes with Keening, Dagoth Ur's shield followed the Heart's strike count, read through his script's member read of the Heart's countHits (on the v0.0.66-dev10 image it read 0). Fixed in v0.0.66-dev11. Before: Found 16 November 2026 (the endgame session ENDGAME-HEART-SESSION-66, run2 on the v0.0.66-dev10 image): Dagoth Ur's script changes his shield ability with the Heart's countHits ("heart_akulakhan".countHits). After the first, second and third Keening strike, which the Heart's own script took (HitOnMe matched 2, 3, 4; PlayGroup 1, 2, 3), dagoth_ur_2->getspell dagoth_ur_shield_02, 03 and 04 each read 0: his script went on reading a count of 0. The object rows are written as u32 reference, u16 id, u16 script, u16 placed, u16 flags (tools/mwscript/awms.py) and AW_MwvmObjectScript reads the script at byte 6, but member() reads it at byte 4, the id; no attached instance has that script, so the read gives 0 and a write is dropped. The v0.0.66-dev10 script file has 186 scripts with 464 reads or writes of another object's local (198 reads, 266 writes), the census clerk's CharGenClassNPC among them. Repair: the script at byte 6, with a native test of a read and a write. Fixed in source on 16 November 2026 (commit 7024bf28 on the v0.0.66 line, not gated yet), covered by tests, to be confirmed by the end-of-quest session on the dev11 image. The interpreter reads the object row through one set of readers (aw_mwvm.c obj_reference, obj_id, obj_script, obj_flags): AW_MwvmObjectScript and the member operations both take the script at byte 6. Tests: tests/test_mwvm_member_native.py with tests/aga_mwvm_member_test.c, on a file the builder's compiler and writer made: a read, a whole-number, a fraction and a short write across two objects with different scripts and an object row whose id is not its script, a script's own variable by its name (its global instance), and the target parked while it is read and written; the unfixed interpreter on the same file read 0 throughout and kept no write. title: A script's SetHealth 0 leaves the actor alive: its health reads 0 but it stays standing and fighting (Dagoth Ur after the end script, the dreamer workers after the Heart)
status: Found 16 November 2026 (the endgame session ENDGAME-HEART-SESSION-66, run2 on the v0.0.66-dev10 image): after the end script's "Dagoth_Ur_2"->SetHealth 0, dagoth_ur_2->gethealth read 0 while the actor list showed him fighting and the console said he cannot reach the player and flees; the three dreamer workers, whose script sets their health to 0 once HeartDestroyed is 1, stayed alive in the list (the end script later hid them). SetHealth sets the base and the current to 0 (AW_ActorSetStat, as OpenMW OpSetDynamic), and host_actor kills only while the base is above 0 (dyn_cur <= 0 and dyn_base > 0). OpenMW 0.51 CreatureStats::setDynamic: a current health under 1 is death, whatever the base. Fixed in source on 16 November 2026 (commit 7024bf28 on the v0.0.66 line, not gated yet), covered by tests, to be confirmed by the end-of-quest session on the dev11 image. One rule for every path, as OpenMW 0.51 (creaturestats.cpp setDynamic, statsextensions.cpp OpSetDynamic): a current health under 1 is death, whatever the base (aw_actorstate.h AW_ACTOR_HEALTH_DEAD). A script's SetHealth, ModHealth or ModCurrentHealth that takes a living NPC or creature under 1 kills it once, as a blow would: the record's death (AW_ActorHealthDeath: OnDeath, the dead count, an essential character's box) and, when its place is loaded, the fight's death or the body a fight leaves (host_actor, as a fall's death does). The same rule now decides a blow's death (aw_combat_rules.c AW_CombatSwing), a spell's and its ticks' (aw_mwhost.c, aw_combat.c AW_CombatSpellHit) and a fall's (aw_fall.c): each killed only at 0 or below before, so an actor left at 0.5 lived. A record already under 1 before the change (a body the data places with no health) is not killed again. Not changed: the player's own death outside a blow (world damage, a script, a spell: at 0 or below, the engine's rule). Tests: tests/test_actor_death_native.py with tests/aga_actor_death_test.c (the real actor record and blow rule): SetHealth 0 on a living actor kills it once; actors taken to 0.5 by SetHealth, ModHealth and ModCurrentHealth die; actors left at 1 live; a dead actor's SetHealth 0 and a body with no health die no second time; a blow that leaves 0.5 kills and one that leaves 1 does not; and the wiring of each path. Reach. Counted in the v0.0.66-dev10 script file (mwscript.awm, SHA-256 e7502ad4336cd1d2): 98 health calls in 57 scripts; 41 set a constant health under 1 in 28 scripts, 39 of them on an NPC or a creature in 26 scripts: EndGame (Dagoth Ur and the seven ash vampires), dreamerWorkerScript, ashvampire, drowned, the six skaalwere scripts, SadriThief, trackerScript, the fabricant and centurion fight (cent_fab_attack, fab_cent_attack, fab_cent_fight_die), ColonyFalco, ErichScript, JeleenScript, ThirskCorpse, ThirskSvenjaDeath, Warlord_aScript, boneScript, drownOnExit and three dialogue results.

title: A script that reads another object's variable can sleep through a change that object's own script makes to it: such a change does not wake quiet scripts
status: Fixed in source on 16 November 2026 (the v0.0.66 line, not gated yet), covered by a test, to be confirmed in a session. Repair chosen: not the readers VOLATILE (they would run every frame) but the targets SHARED: the compiler's whole-program pass marks every script whose variables another script reads (44 scripts of the three masters, the Raven Rock colony scripts and the Heart among them; tools/mwscript/compiler.py, codegen.py SCRIPT_SHARED, the engine's AWS_SHARED), and the interpreter moves the state generation when a SHARED script changes one of its own variables (aw_mwvm.c run), so a quiet reader runs again on the next frame and sees the change; a target that changes nothing wakes nobody. title: A fighter's spell costs it no magicka: the cast's payment names the wrong stat
status: Fixed in source (f42314ab, gate 10959 on ac37e80b) and shipped in v0.0.66-dev12 and v0.0.66; awaiting confirmation in a game: a fight on a numbered build in which a fighter casts a spell and its magicka falls by the cost, and a fighter without enough magicka does not cast. Before: Fixed on the v0.0.66 line (fixed in source and covered by tests, to be confirmed in a game): aw_combat.c start_cast paid the spell with AW_ActorModCurrent(a,1,-cost); stat 1 is Intelligence (AWA_ATTRIBUTE + 1) and AW_ActorModCurrent changes only health, magicka or fatigue, so the call did nothing and a fighter that could afford a spell once cast it every time. The call now names AWA_MAGICKA. aga_combat_test.c has a fighter with magicka for two casts of a 10-point spell: it casts twice, its magicka falls by the cost each time (20, 10, 0), and it casts no third time; the old call fails that test. The only other raw-number call of AW_ActorModCurrent (aw_mwhost.c) passes the script verb's own stat. OpenMW 0.51 takes the cost when the cast starts (worldimp.cpp startSpellCast).

title: The performance guard judges the image step's partition write by the number of partitions and not by their size, so a slowdown back to the old time would pass
status: Found on v0.0.66-dev11 (26ed570f, 16 November 2026) while the image step's partition write was made faster: the build's performance guard judges the step against the median of 62 earlier records of builds with two partitions (v0.0.48-rc1 to v0.0.66-dev10, 43.8 to 96.6 s, small test worlds among them), chosen by the number of partitions and not by how much is written. With the faster writer the step sits near the guard's minimum while the old records keep the median near 66 s, so a slowdown back to about 95 s would pass. Proposed: a time basis per MiB written, or the newest records only, or the records of the same writer version, for steps whose work grows with the data; a test with the old records and a slow new one.

title: A script reading or writing another object's variable walks the instance table and the parking store for the object: with the tables sized for the whole game the walk grows to hundreds of instances and thousands of parked objects, in 307 every-frame operations
status: Found 16 November 2026 in the source (the mwfixes budget sheet, after MWSCRIPT-MEMBER-READS-ID-AS-SCRIPT-66 made the operations reach their objects): aw_mwvm.c member() walked the attached instances (up to 256) and, for a target not attached, the parked objects (up to 2,816) on every GETM, SETM and SETMS; the 99 VOLATILE object scripts of the masters hold 307 such operations (SkinkSoul1 26, WereChangeScript 22), run every frame while their objects are loaded and in range. With the tables sized for the whole game (EXPANSION-SCRIPT-LIMITS-66: 791 instances, 5,478 parked objects) the walk would grow with them. Fixed in source on 16 November 2026 (the v0.0.66 line, not gated yet), covered by tests, to be confirmed in a session: each OBJS row remembers its attached instance (2 bytes a row, set at attach and cleared at detach through a binary search of the rows sorted by reference, 831 rows), and the parking store is hashed by reference (one probe), so every member operation is one step whether the object is attached or parked; the same hash serves the map change (every attach looked its reference up in the store). Not measured in the emulator: the frame share of the scripts is in dbg mwscript status (MWSCRIPT-TICK-SHARE-66), to be read on the dev12 image against dev11. Tests: tests/test_mwvm_limits_native.py (the source rule: member() walks neither table) and tests/test_mwvm_member_native.py (reads and writes of attached and parked targets, unchanged results).
where: engine/aga/src/aw_mwvm.c member (the GETM, SETM and SETMS operations), find_parked, AW_MwvmAttach

title: Raising the fists and pressing V crashed the game: a dynamic light was marked through a negative collision root
status: Repaired in source for v0.0.25-rc8: the model's own visible surface range is lit instead of following a collision root; an address- and undefined-behaviour-checked regression fails on rc7 and passes on the correction. The emulator retest was open when the journal recorded it (2 October 2026) and no later check is recorded. Recorded as an entry from the bug journal on 16 November 2026.
where: renderer: dynamic lights on brush models (R_MarkLights)
severity_reason: the game crashed

history.note: rc7 torch activation crash (rc8 source correction): Reproduction reported by the maintainer: raise fists with F, then press V; game crashes. The successful rc7 native/image build and CI did not detect it. Host reproduction calls the actual brush-render entry point with one active dynamic light and a converted-style model whose collision root is -5. rc7 faults in R_MarkLights while reading node contents before the node array. The retained bm015 fixture contains 42 negative-root brush models; this is valid generated geometry. Positive mesh collision trees can also contain no face references. rc8 therefore lights the model's own visible surface range instead of following either kind of collision root. Surface bounds, local light transforms, model-box rejection, plane distance and tiled-surface exclusion are retained or checked explicitly. The unsigned last-slot mask also avoids signed-shift undefined behavior. The new address/undefined-sanitized regression fails on rc7 and passes on the correction. It exercises R_DrawBEntitiesOnList, not just the standalone lighting helper. Emulator retest remains open. No geometry regeneration, actor waiver, water change or removal of the torch feature is used to bypass the fault.

history.note: Input preflight rejects personal transfer ZIPs — v0.0.25-rc1: Reproduction: put Morrowind_Video.zip and Morrowind_video.zip beside the normal Data Files/Video directory. The scanner previously inventoried every loose file and rejected the case-folded ZIP collision before distinguishing game assets. These are transfer archives, not required game inputs. Fix: positively select Morrowind.esm/Morrowind.bsa by name and supported asset types inside known game folders before path checks, inventory and build hashes. Ignore unrelated directories, root files and transfer archives. Audio inventory counts WAV/MP3 files only. Reference checks use the same game-input selection. Keep normal ESM/BSA checks and ambiguity checks for actual assets. Intro conversion already reads loose Video/mw_intro.bik and never requires a ZIP. Do not modify or rename the maintainer's archives. Synthetic regression covers both differently cased ZIPs, an actual loose video, archive-free input receipts and a real video conflict. No proprietary game files are needed for this host regression.

title: Map loads bypassed the engine's file search paths: a map on an extra world disk image fell back to a whole-file read
status: Repair introduced during v0.0.27-rc3 and included in v0.0.27: the loader opens maps through COM_FOpenFile, records the returned member base and length and seeks relative to it. The loader regressions and the Amiga compile passed; multi-disk gameplay and load-boundary behaviour were still to be verified on the target when the journal recorded it, and no later check is recorded. The journal named it MEM-EXTRA-HDF. Recorded as an entry from the bug journal on 16 November 2026.
where: engine: the streaming map loader and the world-volume search paths
severity_reason: an unexpected map-sized temporary allocation on extra world disk images

history.note: MEM-EXTRA-HDF — map search path bypasses section streaming: Issue: direct com_gamedir fopen cannot find BSPs placed only on additional world-volume search paths; whole-file fallback can add an unexpected BSP-sized temporary allocation. A section-only memory estimate is then insufficient. Affected/observed: path confirmed by inspection of v0.0.27-rc3 loader and world volume wiring; no target crash reproduction claimed for this distinct issue. First introducing version: unverified. Cause: custom streaming loader bypassed the engine filesystem lookup; normal search paths include AW_WORLDn:id1 without changing com_gamedir. Repair source introduced during rc3 and included in v0.0.27 opens through COM_FOpenFile, records the returned member base/length and seeks relative to it. This also respects pack-member offsets. No heap increase or reserve reduction. Verified target-fixed version: pending. Loader direct-byte/offset regressions and the Amiga compile passed; actual multi-HDF gameplay and load-boundary behavior remain to be verified on target. Prevention: audit the actual loader path for every storage layout and retain final-map estimates plus runtime load evidence. See the separate loader trap (docs/MEMORY_ALLOCATION.md).

Cause: src/mwad/masters.py master_path writes the merged master of the selected masters into out/scratch/merged-masters/ of the source tree unless its caller names a folder; the builder's own preflight (tools/build_preflight.py room_grounding_problems, through tools/actor_grounding_census.py room_problems) and the stages call it without one, so --workspace does not move it. Measured: a build started with the source checkout mounted read-only in a container stopped before its first stage with a read-only file system error on the checkout's out folder. A fix moves the folder under the workspace (the build's own scratch); it must not re-key the stages that read the merged master (their keys cover that module).
where: src/mwad/masters.py master_path (the merged master's default folder is out/scratch/merged-masters/ of the source tree), first reached by tools/build_preflight.py room_grounding_problems through tools/actor_grounding_census.py room_problems
severity_reason: Only a build from a read-only source checkout meets it (a build started with the checkout mounted read-only in a container stopped with a read-only file system error naming the checkout's out folder); a writable checkout gets the merged master written inside it, outside the workspace.

title: The strict reuse check counts the units an older version of a bake left in its cache as work the build would redo, so a one-unit table with history stops a build that would reuse it
status: Open; fixed in source in v0.0.67-dev1 (586fd07f, gate 11073); to be confirmed by the first --reuse-all-available build that holds it. The check stopped the engine and image stages with "would bake again 6 of the 7 units its unit cache npc-voice-table holds" while the build needs one table, stored under its unchanged key. Cause: the stop counted the units a cache holds as its largest group under one key; the voice table is looked up once per build and keeps one unit for each set of game files its key saw, each stored by another build. Fix: every stored unit names the build that stored it, and the units one build looks up are the largest group bounded by the most units one build stored under one key (a table: 1; the first-person parts: 579). Measured on the real caches with the release's keys: npc-voice-table 1 of 7 (a stop) becomes 1 of 1; the other caches keep their counts.

title: In the emulator's warp mode the game gets far less processor time per second of its own clock, so its frames take seconds of game time
status: Open, low (the test method, not the game). Measured on the v0.0.66 release image with the opening journey, FS-UAE 3.1.66, JIT 68040 preset, 32 MB Fast. Without warp the engine clock follows the real one (956.5 s in 956.6 s) and the journey passed 42/42. With warp_mode = 1 the engine clock ran 467.6 s in the first 15 host s, the menu frames took 5.6 to 6.6 s of it each and the first map load stopped on the test console folder stall. With uae_warp_limit = 100 (twice a PAL machine's pace) and the deterministic option the menu ran at 1.8 times the real pace, but the start took 46 s (17 s without warp) and the first load's frame 151.0 s of engine clock (5.6 s without warp, the same 470 file calls), about 75 host s against about 6. Cause in the emulator: in warp the processor at its fastest setting runs only within the frame's time base (custom.cpp 1399-1407) and every emulated frame costs host time of its own. Warp is not used to speed up the test sessions; numbers in docs/performance/EMULATOR-WARP.md.
where: FS-UAE 3.1.66 warp mode (custom.cpp 1399-1407, fsuae-events.c 399-404) with the JIT preset at the fastest processor setting
severity_reason: a test method that would have slowed and stalled the scripted sessions; the game itself is not affected and warp is not used for any measurement

title: The CHIM import keys every cell by the master builder request that runs it
status: Found by reading the code on 17 November 2026: the CHIM import's cell key (tools/chimport.py cell_key, the key a whole cell is linked by from the shared storage pool) takes in every AMIWIND_ setting of its process except a short list (CELL_KEY_IGNORED_ENV), and that list leaves out AMIWIND_AW_REQUEST, which the master builder's CHIM import route sets to each request's own id (tools/aw_service.py). The build's own stage keys leave that setting out as bookkeeping (tools/build_cache.py IGNORED_ENV). history.note: Cause, measured on the v0.0.67-dev1 run (read only): the image step's flora support check wrote flora-support.json into the run folder's root, outside every declared stage path. Two stage records name it: the image's own (window 167 to 1043 s) and cell-progress's (window 155 to 210 s, which the file appeared in). The image is never reused, so only cell-progress shows. The fix writes the file into the image's own folder (image/flora-support.json), as its other diagnostics; the check runs once that folder is made, still before the image's slow work. Past the recorded dev1 run: a build reusing it forces cell-progress once (--rebuild-stage cell-progress with --reuse-from; --allow-rebuild cell-progress:BUILD-CELL-PROGRESS-UNDECLARED-OUTPUT-67 with --reuse-all-available): it ran 55 s on one core in the dev1 build, and its output (toolkit/, the tracker data) is read by no later stage, so nothing else runs again. A rule that lets the reuse check pass this one file was not made: it would keep a lasting exception in the undeclared-output check to save under a minute once. It is needed only while that run is the reuse source at the same version: a version change keys cell-progress again anyway (it writes the version).

status: Open; fixed in source on the v0.0.67-dev3 line (fac3d8f7), not yet checked in play. The tile is the foot of the ship's mast: the hold's visual reduction kept the shell's structural shapes whole and reduced the rest to 8 per cent, and the mast (a five-sided column of 30 faces, on the upper deck and again on the lower deck) went to 4 faces while its authored collision column stayed, so the player walked into an invisible post with only the tile at its foot drawn. title: Two texts are drawn on top of each other in the HUD: the name of the aimed character and the place name
status: Open. Seen on the v0.0.66 release: aiming at the clerk of the Census and Excise Office draws his name over the text Seyda Neen at the top right, with the key hint Enter: E under it; the location title of the HUD reads Census and Excise Office, so the second text is not the location title but the label of the door behind the clerk (the exit to Seyda Neen). Cause, read in the engine (engine/aga/src/aw_scene.c AW_SceneDraw): two pickers feed two labels that do not know of each other. The person's name comes from AW_SceneTargetName through npc_target, which takes the nearest person along the view ray (the ray against his model box within reach, FOCUS-NPC-OVERRIDES-ITEM-62), not a radius around the player; it is drawn first, whatever else is aimed. The door label and its action come from aimed_door, whose wall trace ignores people (MOVE_NOMONSTERS), so a door behind a person is aimed through him and its label and action draw in the same corner. Engine-wide, the label of a person therefore competes with the label of whatever else the crosshair meets. Planned rule: one label at a time, the aimed one first: the nearest thing along the view ray among person, door, item and plant decides, and only its label shows; a door behind a person is not aimed. Also a test that fails when two HUD texts share screen space, with a priority order of who yields, built on the shared layout of UI-NO-SHARED-LAYOUT-67.

title: Teleporting to a character in some Tribunal interiors drops the player through the floor (the pawnbroker Ten-Tongues Weerhat, the Assassin)
status: Open; fixed in source on the v0.0.67-opening branch, to be confirmed in play. Cause (found 2026-11-17 by number): a Beings row of the teleport list holds the character's placed point, its feet on the floor, in the room's units. The teleport handed that point to the room load as the arrival, which is the player's origin, 16.875 units over the floor for every door into a room. The arrival search looks for a floor from 8 units over the arrival down to 88 under it, so its first standing box stood inside the floor and it took the next floor under the room, or found none. Measured on the v0.0.67-dev1 image with tools/tp_arrivals.py (all 6,182 room arrivals of the image, the room collision as the image checks read it): from the feet, 1,302 of 3,623 being arrivals land under their floor (base game 1,166 of 3,092, Tribunal 103 of 281, Bloodmoon 33 of 250; Ten-Tongues Weerhat 64 units under the pawnbroker's floor, the Assassin row's room placements 69 under) and 1,553 find no floor. Every teleport to a room (its own start, 1,329) and every door arrival into a room (1,240) lands on its floor in every layer, which is why a teleport to a Tribunal Dwemer ruin works. When the character is in the room at arrival, the teleport then moves the player to a free spot beside it, which can hide the fault; why it showed in Tribunal first is to be confirmed in play. Fix: the engine lifts a being's point to a door arrival's height before the room load (aw_listbox_rules.c AW_TpBeingArrival); with it, 0 of the 6,182 arrivals land under a floor (140 being arrivals still find no standing spot at the point, a cage or a tight corner; they fall back to the room's start and then to the spot beside the character). Guard: tools/tp_arrivals.py on an image (exit 1 on any arrival under its floor) and tests/test_tp_arrivals.py in every gate. The arrival step itself was checked: the room's collision is primed at the arrival before the search runs (the CHIM spawn), and the search does put the player on the floor it finds; the fault was the height it was handed. Outdoors a being's point stays its feet, as the coordinate teleport expects.
where: Every teleport to a person or creature in a room (dbg tp, the Beings choice), in every layer: first seen with Ten-Tongues Weerhat (Tribunal, Mournhold, Pawnbroker, placement 14389) and the Assassin row of Tribunal; 1,302 of the 3,623 being arrivals of the v0.0.67-dev1 image are under their floor

history.note: Cause found. The egg was baked from each effect's own hit model outline, and nine of the fifteen effects in the image (fire, frost, poison, drain, paralyze, light, dispel, turn undead, summon) have hit models with only particles, so their egg fell back to the round dotted sphere; Dagoth Ur's destruction spells are among them (the v0.0.67-dev2 build's magic-effects.json: their bubble is 'sphere', outline 1 x 1). In the whole game data only the shields' hit models are shells around the body (e\magic_hit_S.nif, e\fire_shield.nif, e\lightning_shield.nif, e\frost_shield.nif, about 100 units wide and 150 to 167 tall, from the feet to above the head). The shell was sized from the collision box, which is the same human-sized box for every actor (world.qc aw_npc_floor), so a larger creature's shell (Dagoth Ur's) covered only its middle. The first-person veil, a 26-unit sprite 12 units before the eye, enlarged its dither into a grid of squares across the view, and it kept drawing after a switch to third person because the first-person flag was set when the spell landed. Fix: every effect's egg is baked from the Shield's hit model (tools/prepare_magic.py egg_of, EGG_EFFECT 3) worn with the effect's own texture, with the effect's own hit model laid in at its place on the body; the engine places it by the rule of OpenMW apps/openmw/mwrender/animation.cpp Animation::addEffect: at the actor's feet, at the actor's own scale, a creature fitted to its drawn pose box (aw_magic_rules.c AW_MagicCreatureFit, r_alias.c R_AliasEntityBox); in first person a held shell is a faint tint of the effect's colour (view.c, the power-up palette slot), with the old veil kept as a choice (dbg cast view tint or veil), decided every frame.

title: The actor library stage's two pools wrote their worker share through one temporary file name: a write found its file gone
status: Open: fixed in source. While the creatures bake beside the NPCs, the stage keeps a share file for the NPC pool (the stage's allowance less the creature workers) and rewrites it every half second; when the creatures end, their callback writes it once more from another thread. Both wrote through one temporary file and replaced the share file with it, so the second replace could find the temporary file gone: a build log showed "exception calling callback" with a file-not-found error on that temporary name. The name was the share file's with its suffix replaced, which is also the name the scheduler writes the stage's own allowance through. Fix: one writer at a time (a lock), and a temporary name of the share file's own, with the process number.
where: tools/actor_library.py NpcAllowance.write (the NPC pool's share file beside the stage's allowance file)
severity_reason: the build went on: the failed write was in a callback and the next half-second write put the value right; the same temporary name was also the one the scheduler writes the stage's allowance through, so either writer could lose a write
platform_reason: a build log line of the actor library stage; nothing is drawn

closure.how: a lock around the write and a temporary name of the share file's own; tests/test_actor_library.py writes from six threads beside the callback and expects no error

title: Mournhold's Great Bazaar is under water: the player arrives and walks below a water surface, with the breath bar on, and drowns
status: Open, fixed in source, not seen in play yet. The teleport to the Great Bazaar set the player down about 470 units under its street (at -173 in the original's units; the street is at 297) and so under the water surface at 0 that the game's data gives the districts: the underwater view, the breath bar. The streets are above the water (25 to 297); only the canal and the sunken parts lie below it, as in the original. Cause: at the moment a teleport with a height looks for the first surface at or below that height, the street's collision is not loaded yet in this district, and the search ends far below. Fix in source: such a landing holds the player at the asked point until the floor under it is loaded (aw_arrival_hold). See the dated notes.
where: the Mournhold test build of 104174ce (the first build with Mournhold's five outdoor districts): dbg tp greatbazaar and a walk there show a blue tint, the water surface from below and the breath bar running out (arrival local z -43 and -49 in the district's map mh0002). In Tribunal's data all five districts are flagged as having water but give no water height; the engine puts the surface at height 0, as OpenMW reads such a flag. The Great Bazaar's streets lie below 0 and the Plaza Brindisi Dorom's floor just above it (a water plane at its feet). The districts lie outside the regular map area of the game, so the normal water level should not apply there; the original has no water in these streets.
severity_reason: a whole district of the city is unplayable: the player drowns in the Great Bazaar; the maintainer set it as P0

closure.why: A teleport whose first landing is far under its asked height searches at the asked point at once and takes a higher spot beside it only when no other exists: dbg tp greatbazaar lands on the street (the cause was the Plaza gate wall beside the point, not a late-loading street); fix 2b1bc8db; not yet seen in play.

history.note: Measured on the test image's own collision, in the original's units: in the Great Bazaar's western cell the surfaces a player can stand on lie between 25 and 297, none of them under 0; the street under the arrival point is at 297. The player in the stills stood at about -173: 470 units under the street and 173 under the water. The water surface at 0 is what the game's data gives: the five districts carry the water flag and no water height, and an open-source engine for the game draws that as a surface at 0. It fills what the districts build below their streets: Godsreach's canal bed at -321, a basin in the bazaar's eastern cell at -106, the Plaza's at -46, the Temple's moat at -146. The district frames do not shift heights. So the district is not flooded: the teleport leaves the player under the street, where there is nothing to stand on and the water is all around. The other four districts' arrivals stand on their streets. Not proven yet: why this arrival ends under the floor (the street's collision not there yet when the player is set down, or the gate leaf 13 units from the arrival point pushing him off the spot); the next in-game check reads the first arrival, a second arrival from inside the district and the game's own standing search by number. Registered at first as TP-BAZAAR-ARRIVAL-UNDER-FLOOR-67, closed as a duplicate of this entry.

The arrival read second by second on the same test image: one second after the teleport by the district's name the eye is at frame-local -53 (the street is at 74) and it stays there: the player is set down low at once, he does not fall. The same with the step-off from a body switched off (-46), with the same point typed as coordinates with its height (-42), and 60 units further into the street, away from the gate and from the border between the district's two cells (-36). The point's x and y without a height finds no floor at all and falls back to the frame's start point, where the player stands on the street (eye 106). Some seconds later the game's own standing search finds the street at the arrival point. So the street's collision is not in the ring yet at the moment a teleport with a height looks for the first surface at or below that height; the search goes past the place where the street comes a moment later and ends far below, under the water surface. The other four districts have their floors loaded at that moment and their arrivals stand. Why the Great Bazaar's street comes late is not found yet (its frames are the heaviest of the districts beside the Plaza's). An earlier reading of mine, that a second arrival from inside the district ruled this out, was wrong: a teleport loads the map again. Fix in source (engine/aga/src/aw_scene.c, aw_arrival_hold 1): the asked height names the floor, so a landing more than 64 units below it holds the player at the asked point without gravity while the ring loads; each frame asks the standing-spot rule for the floor under the point and the first answer sets the player down; after 8 seconds without a floor the first landing is kept (a point over deep ground or open water lands as before, 8 seconds later). Not seen in play yet: the next test image shows the console line "Arrival: the floor is loaded" and the arrival's height.

title: tools/build.py --check cannot check the reuse plan of a workspace that is mounted read-only: its build preflight stops on the cache folders it cannot write before the reuse plan is made
status: Open (18 November 2026). Measured: tools/build.py --check, with and without --reuse-from, against a development workspace and the game data both mounted read-only (and the source tree read-only) stopped after about 90 s in its build preflight, before the reuse plan: tools/build_preflight.py counted every folder of WORKSPACE/cache the build user cannot write (135,451) as a problem, and the room grounding check failed writing the merged master into the checkout (out/scratch, BUILD-MERGED-MASTER-IN-CHECKOUT-66). A check writes no stage index, but it keeps the unit census and the pre-flight analysis in the workspace cache, so it cannot run on a workspace one may only read (a shared or archived one). The stage plan alone runs read only: tools/build.py --reuse-plan RUN and tools/reuse_all.py predict. A fix: a --check reports unwritable cache folders as a note (the build keeps its stop) and writes no cache bookkeeping, and the merged master leaves the checkout (BUILD-MERGED-MASTER-IN-CHECKOUT-66).
where: tools/build_preflight.py run (the cache folder check) as tools/build.py --check runs it before the reuse plan; src/mwad/masters.py master_path (the merged master in the checkout)
severity_reason: Only a check against a read-only workspace meets it: a build needs a writable cache anyway, and tools/build.py --reuse-plan RUN and tools/reuse_all.py predict give the stage plan of such a workspace read only.

title: A default build with expansions selected took none of their finished outdoor cells: the cell list was resolved before the expansions were selected
status: Open: fixed in source. Since v0.0.65 the default cell list was meant to add each selected expansion's named set of cells (Solstheim's for Bloodmoon; Mournhold's districts for Tribunal since the v0.0.67 work), taking the cells the progress tracker calls finished. The list is resolved before the game data check, and the selection was read from the value that check records, so the masters were always empty there and no set was ever added: a test build with all three game files selected listed 1,348 cells in 1,348 frames and 61 dropped, the base list alone, and its plan held no stage for the districts. The unit tests set the recorded value themselves, so they passed. Until then no expansion cell was finished in the tracker, so no earlier build lost anything. Fix: the base world's cell list takes no expansion's set at all (an expansion's cells are built by its own module; Mournhold's districts by the module tribunal-mournhold), the module reads the selection itself, and a first-minute check (expansion-module-cells) names for each selected expansion how many cells the tracker calls finished and which module builds them, and stops the build when finished cells would be left out without a stated reason. To do: confirm in the next test build's first lines (the module's line with 11 district cells, the check's line, the two module stages in the plan).

title: The image's door tables knew only the Vvardenfell world's frames: with Mournhold's districts as a world of their own, every door into or out of a district would have stayed closed
status: Open: fixed in source. The world door table and the room batches' door links resolve an exterior door or arrival by one holder rule: the town frame whose box holds the point, else the region frame of its cell. The region frames came from the Vvardenfell world's table alone, and the planned cells from the exterior checklist alone. Mournhold's districts are built by the module tribunal-mournhold as a world of their own and installed as a store of their own, so none of their frames was a holder and their cells were not planned: each district door would have been listed as held back. Fix: both tables also take the frames of the worlds the image installs as stores of their own, under the frame map names their install gives them (tools/chim/layer_stores.py frame_holders), and count those cells as planned. To do: read the "Presented districts" line of the first image that holds the districts (doors linked and still held back), and walk a door in each direction in game.

title: The stage of Mournhold's districts was keyed by its own unit cache folder: the units a run stored re-keyed the stage for the next run
status: Open: fixed in source. The check of a build that resumes a failed one stopped on "the stage would run again ... because its key changed: external_inputs". The stage's only input outside the run folder is its own unit cache folder; the key hashed the folder's files, and the failed run had itself stored its units there (4,076 files), so the run's own key no longer matched. The outdoor world stage's unit cache has been exempt from this since BUILD-CACHE-CHIM-UNITS-33 (every unit there is found by its own key and verified); the new stage's cache was not listed. Fix: the stage's cache is listed as content-addressed, and its row is in the key from the stage's first run on, before the folder exists, so making the folder moves no key either. Open beside it: the other content-addressed caches get their row only once their folder exists; their keys were left as they are.

title: In first person the Nord man, the Imperial woman and the Dark Elf and Redguard men show another race's or sex's hand, as the game's records name it, and the skin steps at the wrist
status: Fixed in source (8308ba5a and f1a962c2 on branch v0.0.67-fpfist, gate 11741); to be confirmed in play on an image built with it. Decided for the project, 2026-11-18: every race and sex draws its own first-person hand, assembled from its own parts through the existing first-person parts pipeline, and no steep colour step at any seam of the arm, whatever the race. A deliberate departure from the original's data, which OpenMW follows: four of the game's first-person hand records name another race's or sex's mesh: b_n_nord_m_hands.1st names b\B_N_Imperial_M_Hands.1st.nif, b_n_imperial_f_hands.1st names b\B_N_Nord_F_Hands.1st.nif, b_n_dark elf_m_hand.1st names b\B_N_Dark Elf_F_Hands.1st.NIF and b_n_redguard_m_hands.1st names b\B_N_Redguard_F_Hands.1st.nif (Morrowind.esm; not changed by Tribunal or Bloodmoon). The game's archive holds each one's own first-person hand mesh (b\b_n_nord_m_hands.1st.nif, b\b_n_imperial_f_hands.1st.nif, b\b_n_dark elf_m_hands.1st.nif, b\b_n_redguard_m_hands.1st.nif: the same 580 triangles, its own skin textures), used by no record; the builder takes that own mesh for these four. The rest of the part table is the race's own records by the original's and OpenMW's order (the sex's first-person part, then its third-person one, then for a woman the man's; the one fallback is the Argonian woman's forearm, the man's). The seam step between the hand and the wrist part, as drawn on the v0.0.67-dev2 image, was up to 55 per channel (the Nord man); with the race's own hand skins it is still up to 40 for some races (the Khajiit woman), and the game's own wrist and forearm parts step by up to 37 (the Khajiit man): the colours are matched along the arm at each seam (the wrist to the forearm, the hand to the wrist), on by default, behind a builder switch whose other setting keeps the original's parts as they are. The measured tables are in FP-BARE-HAND-OTHER-SKIN-67's history.

severity_reason: the player's own hands look like another race's in every scene for four of the twenty race and sex choices, and a steep colour step shows at the wrist for several more

title: After the race or sex is changed several times in one place, the first-person arms turn into an old hand model with holes and the held lantern is not drawn
status: Fixed in source (8308ba5a and f1a962c2 on branch v0.0.67-fpfist, gate 11741): a part model that leaves its set is released at once unless a set still draws it, a refused slot holds off only that outfit, and a race or sex change by any path releases both old sets; to be confirmed in play on an image built with it. Cause read from the session's console (the v0.0.67-dev2 image with the engine of gate 11689, the light test corridor, the race and sex switched in place through Argonian, Breton, Dark Elf, High Elf and Imperial, man and woman each): at the switch to the Khajiit the engine printed "First-person arms from parts: no model slot for progs/parts/cb/619564a20d.mdl (slot 6)" and the same for all eight of the Khajiit's arm parts, then "no part loaded: the baked arms draw", "Hand model slots unavailable; using legacy models" and "First-person held light: no light stance in the arms from parts". From then on, for every later race, the first person drew the legacy hand model (the jagged hand with holes) and no held light (the light rides the arms from parts). Why: the first-person parts are optional models, admitted only while the engine's model table is under its static base or a released slot is free (model.c Mod_CanFindName); every race and sex loads 8 new arm parts and 21 body parts, the parts of the old set are unpinned but never released (aw_view.c hand_parts_ready and parts_ready), and the third-person body loads its parts without that check and grows the table; and one refusal turns the arms from parts off for the whole session (hparts_failed is never reset by a race or outfit change).

title: In Mournhold's districts no container, item, activator or door sign can be aimed at: their rows are keyed as a room's, and the game outdoors asks for the cells around the player
status: Open: fixed in source, not yet seen in the game. Cause: in the game data a district is an interior cell, and the three readers that key placed things by area gave its rows the cell's room number at the original positions. The build presents a district as a block of exterior cells, so the game there is outdoors and asks for the exterior cells around the player: every aim in a courtyard read no rows. By number on the test build's game files: 319 focus rows sat under the five room numbers (Godsreach 73, the Great Bazaar 136, Plaza Brindisi Dorom 47, the Royal Palace courtyard 48, the Temple courtyard 15) and none under the 11 cells of the blocks. Fix: with the build module for the districts, the readers take the districts' cells from one new function (`prepare_focus.cells_presented`), which gives each presented cell as the cells of its block with every placement moved by the one move the presented world itself gets; the focus and item-models stages take the module's receipt and wait for its data stage. The same 319 rows are then under the blocks' keys, the other 2634 keys hold the same rows, and 1212 moved placements equal the presented master's own bytes. A first-minute check holds the counts per district against the districts' own cells, and without the module every reader gives what it gave before (held by tests). To do: on the next test build, open a container, take an item and read an activator in two districts.
